merged.title: JWT session cookie never refreshes: every member is hard signed out 30 days after sign-in, regardless of activity
merged.reasoning: Verified against the installed next-auth source. The app's exported auth = cache(guardedSession), and guardedSession calls nextAuth.auth() with NO arguments (src/lib/auth.ts:428). In node_modules/next-auth/lib/index.js the no-args branch is the RSC path: `return getSession(_headers, _config).then(parseSessionResponse)` — parseSessionResponse only reads the response BODY and discards the Set-Cookie headers the session action emits for the rolling refresh. Only the isReqWrapper (middleware/route) and API-route branches copy Set-Cookie onto the response, and this app uses neither: there is no middleware.ts (proxy.ts only checks cookie existence), no SessionProvider and no useSession anywhere in src (grep confirmed both), so GET /api/auth/session is never fetched. session:{strategy:'jwt'} at auth.ts:256-258 sets no maxAge, so the @auth/core default 30d applies (dev-login's MAX_AGE=30d corroborates). Net: the JWT exp and cookie Expires are fixed at sign-in+30d and never advance on activity — an absolute session, not the rolling/idle session NextAuth documents. Real and member-visible (a forced re-login ~30 days after sign-in regardless of use, a synchronized wave for a launch cohort), but downgraded to Low: it is a recoverable re-login with no data loss, and a 30-day absolute session is a defensible posture, so whether to add rolling refresh is a product call, not a crash/corruption. Minor related drift: dev-login/route.ts:42 'Matches the session.maxAge in src/lib/auth.ts' — auth.ts sets no maxAge; it matches the library default.
merged.repro: Code trace: sign-in mints the cookie via POST /api/auth/callback (handlers route). Every subsequent request resolves identity through auth()->nextAuth.auth() (no args) -> RSC branch -> parseSessionResponse drops Set-Cookie, so no refresh cookie is ever applied. With default maxAge 30d and nothing hitting /api/auth/session (no useSession/SessionProvider) and no middleware, the cookie Expires stays at sign-in+30d. Live confirmation if wanted: sign in, record __Secure-authjs.session-token Expires, browse/run server actions, re-read the cookie — Expires unchanged.
merged.fix: Product decision. To restore rolling sessions, refresh the cookie from a context that can write it (a real NextAuth middleware, or wrap authenticated route handlers so the wrapper branch reapplies Set-Cookie), or shorten/lengthen maxAge deliberately. If 30-day absolute is accepted, document it and fix the dev-login:42 comment that references a non-existent maxAge.
merged.gate: An e2e assertion that navigates after sign-in and checks the session cookie Expires advances (fails today), or a documented, comment-anchored decision to keep absolute 30-day sessions.

merged.title: Blocked member can complete the password-reset flow and is told 'we are signing you in now', then every sign-in refuses with 'Invalid email or password' — an endless misleading loop
merged.reasoning: Traced end to end. requestPasswordReset (email-actions.ts:258-261) selects id/name/email/password only — no isBlocked — and enqueues a real reset mail for any row with a password. resetPassword (email-actions.ts:373-444) also never reads isBlocked: it writes the new password, stamps emailVerified, increments credentialVersion, mints a human pass, and returns {ok:true}. reset-client.tsx then shows 'That's done ... we are signing you in now' (reset-client.tsx:187-189) and calls signIn('credentials',...). authorize() (auth.ts:185-192) is the ONLY isBlocked gate: it runs AFTER a correct bcrypt compare and returns null, which the login client maps to the generic 'Invalid email or password', and reset-client.tsx:143 then bounces to /login where the new password is refused again — an endless misleading loop. Mechanism confirmed; no isBlocked reference exists anywhere in email-actions.ts. Downgraded to Low: it requires an admin to have blocked the account and that (deliberately excluded) person to run a reset; the outcome is confusion, not data loss — the password/credentialVersion writes on a blocked row are harmless.
merged.repro: Create a throwaway account via signup; block it in admin; run forgot-password -> reset-password with a new password. resetPassword returns ok and the page says 'signing you in now'; the immediate signIn returns ok:false (auth.ts:191) and every manual login also shows 'Invalid email or password'. emailVerified and credentialVersion on the blocked row are updated by the reset.
merged.fix: Add an isBlocked check to the reset flow: either short-circuit requestPasswordReset for blocked rows (keeping the same {ok:true} to preserve the membership oracle) and/or refuse in resetPassword before the transaction, returning copy that does not promise a sign-in the door will refuse.
merged.gate: Integration test: block a user, then assert requestPasswordReset enqueues no reset mail for that row and/or resetPassword does not return an auto-sign-in success for a blocked account.

merged.title: Three auth clients await server actions with no try/catch — a rejected action strands the form on a disabled busy button forever (the exact B-042 class already fixed elsewhere with callAction)
merged.reasoning: Confirmed on all three surfaces. reset-client.tsx:116-117 (setBusy(true) then `const result = await resetPassword(...)`), forgot-client.tsx:69/90 (setSending(true) then `await requestPasswordReset(formData)`), and verify-client.tsx:108-114 (handleResend: setBusy(true) then `await resendVerification()` with no try/finally) all await a server action with no try/catch. A rejected action (dropped network, deploy skew where the server-action id 404s, an uncaught server 500) rejects the await; the code after it — every setBusy(false)/setSending(false)/setError — never runs, and no error boundary catches event-handler rejections, so the button sits on 'Saving...'/'Sending...' disabled until a full reload. This is exactly the B-042 class already fixed with callAction in verify-email-banner.tsx:97 (try/finally) and with try/catch in login-client.tsx:365-428 and signup-form.tsx. The three auth surfaces were left out. Downgraded to Low: recovery is a page reload and the trigger is a fault condition, not the normal path; the reset-client instance is the worst because it compounds with C-035 (a post-commit throw leaves the member unsure their password actually changed).
merged.repro: In devtools set network offline, load /reset-password with a valid token and submit: the button stays on 'Saving...' with no message and an unhandled-rejection in console; only reload recovers. Same on /forgot-password ('Sending...') and the /verify-email resend button ('Sending...').
merged.fix: Route each await through callAction() as verify-email-banner.tsx:97 does, or wrap in try/catch and move the busy reset into a finally, matching login-client.tsx.
merged.gate: A pattern guard (or targeted test) that these three handlers dispatch server actions via callAction/try-catch, same as the B-042 fix.

merged.title: resetPassword awaits two post-commit writes with no catch, so a transient DB error after the password has changed turns success into a thrown action — and the adjacent comment claims the opposite ('never awaited for success')
merged.reasoning: Confirmed both halves. After the burn-token-plus-set-password transaction commits (email-actions.ts:373-409), resetPassword plainly `await`s burnTokens (line 424), enqueueMail (line 431) and mintHumanPass (line 442) with no try/catch. enqueueMail (email-queue.ts:438-479) performs awaited prisma.outboundEmail.findFirst + count + create, any of which throws on a pool/network error, so a transient DB fault AFTER the password has been written propagates out of the 'use server' function — turning a committed success into a thrown action, skipping mintHumanPass, while the token is already burned (a retry then says 'That link has already been used'). Combined with C-034's missing client catch, the member sees 'Saving...' forever and cannot tell the password changed. Second half: the comment at email-actions.ts:429-430 states the mail is 'never awaited for success: a mail failure must not undo a password change that has already been written', but the code literally `await`s it — a genuine comment-vs-code drift (contrast requestPasswordReset:278-291 which correctly defers the same enqueue inside after()). Low: the window is narrow (a DB error between commit and return) and rare, but real and unconditional in mechanism.
merged.repro: Code trace is sufficient: $transaction at line 373 commits; lines 424/431/442 are unguarded awaits; enqueueMail (email-queue.ts:464/470) issues awaited DB writes that reject on a pool/network error, propagating past the committed password change. To demo, force a throw in enqueueMail after the transaction on a scratch branch and run the reset: password changes, client sticks on 'Saving...'.
merged.fix: Wrap the post-commit writes (burnTokens, enqueueMail, mintHumanPass) in try/catch that logs, or move them behind after(), so a best-effort failure cannot convert the committed success into a thrown action; then make the comment and code agree.
merged.gate: Unit test that forces the post-commit enqueueMail to reject and asserts resetPassword still resolves {ok:true} rather than throwing.

merged.title: A mail scanner's GET auto-confirms an email address: /verify-email redeems the token during render, so a hostile signup with someone else's address is 'confirmed' by the victim's link-scanning gateway without any human click
merged.reasoning: Confirm-on-GET is a documented, deliberate design decision: verify-email/page.tsx:7-18 states the token is 'redeemed during render rather than behind a button' because 'a confirmation page with a confirm button on it asks somebody to click twice', and the prefetch case was already handled gracefully (B-021/Low-22: used->already/superseded). The finder's novel 'hostile signup with the victim's address' angle grants the attacker no capability they lack otherwise: the confirmation email is delivered to the VICTIM's mailbox (which the attacker does not control), and email-confirmation only lifts the Stage-1 gate (posting/uploads) that the attacker could obtain anyway by confirming their OWN address. The victim is not a member and experiences only a stray email; Stage-2 verification and admin review still gate contact details (finder concedes this bounds it). Per the false-positive exclusions this is a deliberate decision plus a speculative consequence with no concrete member-visible harm — REFUTED. State-changing GET on email confirmation is an industry-standard trade-off, not a defect here.

merged.gate: Extend valley-day.test.mjs's timezone sweep to assert member-facing IST clock times carry a zone label, and/or a comment-accuracy check on sendTimeLabel.

merged.title: Pasting a full Instagram URL stores it verbatim and renders a double-prefixed dead link
merged.reasoning: social.ts:14 `if (kind === "instagram") return https://instagram.com/${v.replace(/^@/, "")}` sits ABOVE the http(s) prefix check at line 15, so a stored value like `https://instagram.com/ananya` becomes `https://instagram.com/https://instagram.com/ananya`. Nothing normalizes instagram on write: updateContactMethods (profile-actions.ts:326) stores `parsed.data.instagram` verbatim; contactMethodsSchema (validators.ts:187) only caps it at 100 chars (a full IG URL is ~28 chars, fits); contacts-editor.tsx has an `@handle` placeholder but no normalization. The profile page builds the Instagram method from socialHref/socialDisplay at page.tsx:256-261, so the dead link and the `@https://instagram.com/ananya` display ship on the public profile. linkedin/facebook/website avoid this because they fall through to the http check. Downgraded High->Medium: real and hit on a normal-ish path (pasting a full URL) but bounded to one social link, self-correctable, and the placeholder nudges toward a handle.
merged.repro: Code trace: socialHref('instagram','https://instagram.com/ananya') = 'https://instagram.com/https://instagram.com/ananya'; socialDisplay('instagram','https://instagram.com/ananya') = '@https://instagram.com/ananya'. No write-side normalizer exists (profile-actions.ts:326, contactMethodsSchema validators.ts:187, contacts-editor.tsx). Behavioral: save 'https://instagram.com/ananya' in the Instagram row, open Get in touch, inspect the anchor href.
merged.fix: Normalize the instagram value on write (strip a leading http(s)://instagram.com/ and any @ before storing) OR make socialHref honor an http(s) prefix for instagram too (move the instagram branch below the startsWith('http') check, extracting the trailing path segment). Apply the same normalize at contactMethodsSchema/contacts-editor so the stored column is always a bare handle.
merged.gate: Unit test on socialHref/socialDisplay + a write-side normalizer test: a pasted 'https://instagram.com/x' resolves to a working 'https://instagram.com/x' href and '@x' display.

merged.title: adminUpdatePerson writes batchYear without re-deriving batchType, so the credential drifts and batch-targeted visibility breaks
merged.reasoning: adminUpdatePerson (admin/people/actions.ts:127-138) writes {name, accountType, batchYear, birdOverride} and never re-derives batchType, whereas updateProfileField (profile-actions.ts:188-198) explicitly reads the stored year pair and recomputes data.batchType = batchTypeFromLeaving(...) 'so the credential can never drift out of step with the years'. batchTargetKey (post-visibility-rule.ts:88-98, used at :227) combines batchType (board: ISC/ICSE) with a 4-digit batchYear. formatBatch (utils.ts:204) reads only batchYear, so the byline stays correct and masks the drift. The real consequence is narrow: when an admin batchYear correction moves the (batchYear - yearLeft) gap across the ICSE/ISC boundary, the stored batchType (board) becomes wrong, so the viewer's batch key is e.g. 'ISC-2012' when it should be 'ICSE-2012' and batch-targeted posts reach the wrong set. Also true: adminUpdatePerson never calls tryRosterAutoVerifyQuietly on a batchYear fix (updateProfileField does at :206-208), and an accountType flip here leaves stray tenure/batch fields. Downgraded Medium->Low: requires an admin edit that crosses the board boundary plus a batch-targeted post; the visible byline is unaffected.
merged.repro: Row with yearLeft=2010, batchYear=2010 => batchType='ISC' (12th-grade leaver). Admin corrects batchYear to 2012 via the person page (member's cohort graduated 2012 but they left 2010 => should be ICSE). adminUpdatePerson writes batchYear=2012 but leaves batchType='ISC'. batchTargetKey now yields 'ISC-2012' instead of 'ICSE-2012'; a post targeting 'ICSE-2012' will not reach them and 'ISC-2012' wrongly will.
merged.fix: In adminUpdatePerson, when batchYear changes, read the row's yearLeft and set batchType = batchTypeFromLeaving(yearLeft, batchYear) (null-safe, mirroring profile-actions.ts:188-198); consider firing tryRosterAutoVerifyQuietly on a batch/name change, and deciding whether an accountType flip should clear batch/tenure fields.
merged.gate: Unit/integration test asserting batchType is consistent with (yearLeft, batchYear) after adminUpdatePerson for an ICSE/ISC-boundary edit.

merged.title: Onboarding register step bypasses the shared place validation all other UserPlace writers use
merged.reasoning: saveOnboardingRegister (onboarding/actions.ts:22-40, 78-106) uses a LOCAL placeSchema: `placeId: z.number().int().nullable()` (no .positive(), never checked against the Place table), `lat/lng: z.number().nullable()` (no -90..90 / -180..180 bounds), and `places: max(20)`. The other two writers -- updateUserPlaces (settings/actions.ts:153-158) and adminUpdatePlaces (admin/people/actions.ts:164-169) -- both route through parsePlaces + resolvePlaces (place-input.ts), which bounds coordinates, requires positive placeIds, verifies them against the table, and NULLs unknown ids so a stale/bad id degrades to a free-typed place instead of a P2003 FK abort. Onboarding's tx.userPlace.createMany passes p.placeId as given (UserPlace.place is an FK), so an invalid placeId aborts the whole transaction, losing admission number/occupation/org/cities in one save. The place-input.ts:19 doc claim 'all three writers share one definition' is factually false for onboarding -- a real comment-vs-code drift. Downgraded Medium->Low: the LocationPicker only supplies real gazetteer ids/coords, so the FK abort and out-of-range coords need a stale id or a crafted payload; the firmest defect is the divergence + inaccurate doc.
merged.repro: Diff onboarding/actions.ts:22-28 (local schema, no bounds/positive/resolvePlaces) vs place-input.ts:24-38, 73-88. saveOnboardingRegister({places:[{placeId:999999999,label:'X',city:'X',lat:null,lng:null}]}) hits the UserPlace->Place FK and throws P2003 out of the action with nothing saved; the same payload through updateUserPlaces degrades placeId to null and saves. lat 9999 passes the local schema and lands in UserPlace.
merged.fix: Replace the local placeSchema/createMany in saveOnboardingRegister with parsePlaces + resolvePlaces (the shared place-input helpers), and align the cap to MAX_PLACES (30). Either way, correct the place-input.ts:19 comment or make onboarding genuinely share the definition.
merged.gate: Unit test that all three place writers reject out-of-range coordinates and null an unknown placeId rather than throwing; a test that saveOnboardingRegister degrades an unknown placeId.

merged.title: Places autosave fires an unserialized wipe-and-recreate per edit: overlapping saves lose data or show a false connection error
merged.reasoning: useAutoSave.run (pen.tsx:348-371) only counts inFlight; it never queues or serializes, and commitPlaces (letterhead-profile.tsx:429-438) fires updateUserPlaces on every LocationPicker change with no ordering token. updateUserPlaces is a wipe-and-recreate $transaction; the @@unique([userId,position]) (schema.prisma:767-775) is a DELIBERATE guard that aborts the losing overlapping transaction, so the serious double-insert corruption is already prevented. The residual, real defects: (1) on abort the loser's promise rejects, run()'s catch sets state='error' with 'That did not save. Check your connection.' while setPlaces(next) already put the newer list on screen and router.refresh only runs on success -- screen and DB diverge until a manual reload; (2) two non-overlapping out-of-order completions (network reordering) both succeed and the earlier-intent list can silently win. Downgraded Medium->Low: corruption is guarded by the unique; the residual is a misleading message + rare silent revert needing a reload, and the trigger is two saves inside one network RTT.
merged.repro: commitPlaces at :429 calls void run(updateUserPlaces(next)) without awaiting the prior run; run() (pen.tsx:348-361) has no queue. Two rapid city edits dispatch two concurrent wipe-recreate transactions; the unique aborts one, run() surfaces 'That did not save' while the screen holds the newer list and the DB holds the loser's list (no router.refresh on failure).
merged.fix: Serialize commits in useAutoSave (chain each run() onto the previous promise, or coalesce trailing calls), and add an ordering precondition to updateUserPlaces (e.g. an updatedAt token like editPost) so a stale save cannot overwrite a newer one; on failure, re-fetch (router.refresh) so the screen reconverges with the DB.
merged.gate: e2e or unit test that two queued place saves converge on the last-submitted list and never leave the error banner with a divergent on-screen list.

merged.title: Roster import's --match-existing backfill verifies members without stamping verifyStateAt
merged.reasoning: The backfill UPDATE in scripts/dev/import-roster.mjs:199-203 sets verifyState='verified', verifyMethod='office_list', verifiedAt=now() but omits verifyStateAt. schema.prisma:53 mandates 'STAMP THIS WHENEVER YOU WRITE verifyState'; verifyStateAt defaults to now() at row creation (schema.prisma:66) and is never updated here, so a script-verified member keeps their signup-era timestamp. admin-worklist-query.ts orders the recently-verified/oldest lists by verifyStateAt (lines 84 desc, 94 asc) and serializes u.verifyStateAt.toISOString() (157/165), so the import batch is mis-sorted and the 'recently verified' view never surfaces it. Low: this is a manually-run admin import script and the only consequence is admin worklist sort order, not member-facing behavior.
merged.repro: After --apply --match-existing: SELECT id, "verifyState", "verifiedAt", "verifyStateAt" FROM "User" WHERE "verifyMethod"='office_list' AND "verifiedAt" > "verifyStateAt" returns the script-verified rows; admin-worklist-query.ts:84/94 sorts by the stale verifyStateAt.
merged.fix: Add "verifyStateAt" = now() to the UPDATE at import-roster.mjs:200-201, matching the four Prisma writers (verification-actions.ts:55, admin-actions.ts:160/206, roster.ts:81).
merged.gate: A grep/lint or unit assertion that every writer of verifyState in the same statement also writes verifyStateAt (the invariant in schema.prisma:53).

merged.title: Three different admission-number ceilings: 10000 in onboarding/settings schemas, 100000 in the profile editor
merged.reasoning: updateProfileField (profile-actions.ts:111) accepts admission numbers up to 100000, while registerStepSchema (onboarding/actions.ts:31) and profileSchema (validators.ts:164) both cap the same User.admissionNumber column at 10000. This is the exact validator-cap-drift class (audit Low 84). merged.title: Profile pen accepts years up to 2100 that every other writer refuses
merged.reasoning: updateProfileField's YEAR_MAX is a flat 2100 (profile-actions.ts:28-29, :135), so batchYear/yearJoined/yearLeft up to 2100 save through the live inline editor, and yearClash (profile-actions.ts:229-246) only checks relative ordering. So a typo like batchYear 2099 saves on the profile and renders (formatBatch utils.ts:204 reads batchYear; parseBatchYear accepts up to LAST_BATCH_YEAR=2100 per batch-year.ts:25/46, so directory tiles/filters accept it too), where every schema-based form refuses it. yearClash also does not cover batchYear<yearJoined with yearLeft empty. merged.title: Concurrent avatar upload/remove races orphan R2 objects that nothing can ever find again
merged.reasoning: updateAvatar (settings/actions.ts:225-262) does putImage(new)->read prev->update photoUrl->delImage(prev) with no transaction or precondition. Two overlapping uploads both putImage (urlA, urlB in R2), both read prev=old, both update (last writer, say urlB, wins), both delImage(old). urlA is then referenced by no row and deleted by nothing -- the exact TRAPS H9 orphan ('bytes survive its own deletion, silently and for ever, and nothing anywhere reports it'). removeAvatar (:264-280) racing an upload has the same shape: it nulls photoUrl and deletes old, orphaning the upload's new object. This also contradicts the in-code claim at :214 that 'storage never grows (the prior avatar is deleted on replace)'. Low: bounded by the uploads rate limit and requires concurrent uploads (two tabs, or a retry racing a slow first call); cost/leak, not correctness or member-visible.
merged.repro: Trace settings/actions.ts:250-258: the losing request's freshly-uploaded url is only ever held in that request's memory; it is never the final photoUrl and never passed to delImage. Dev (filesystem storage): fire two updateAvatar in one Promise.all with different files and list public/uploads/avatars/<id>/ -- two objects, one referenced.
merged.fix: Make the swap atomic: read prev and update in one transaction with an updatedAt/version precondition, or record the superseded url in PendingImagePurge so a sweep can reclaim a raced orphan; delete the old object only after the update that references the new one commits as the current row.
merged.gate: Unit/integration test that after two concurrent updateAvatar calls exactly one avatar object remains referenced and none is orphaned; correct the :214 comment.

merged.title: Onboarding photo step still ships the uncropped photo into the server's blind centre crop
merged.reasoning: The onboarding photo step (photo-step.tsx:39-76) calls shrinkForUpload then updateAvatar directly with NO crop dialog (no AvatarCropDialog import or mount). updateAvatar's server pipeline does a fixed resize(512,512,{fit:'cover',position:'centre'}) (settings/actions.ts:238), so an off-centre face is centre-cropped for every new member's first upload. merged.title: Revoking the Keeper hat overwrites a legacy group-admin role with 'member', silently stripping group moderation
merged.reasoning: Confirmed setCatchupKeeper revoke (actions.ts:1947-1950) runs updateMany({ where:{ groupId, userId }, data:{ role: 'member' } }) with no role predicate, so a target whose GroupMember row is 'admin' (the group's own admin role, which isEffectiveKeeper honours and which deletePost reads for group-post moderation, per the isEffectiveKeeper docblock catchups.ts:340-355) is demoted to 'member' as a side effect of toggling the Keeper hat off — the opposite of the grant direction, which deliberately writes 'keeper' to preserve the decoupling (docblock :1917-1930). merged.title: Extending the deadline of a dormant Round extends from the long-dead deadline: success reported, nothing changes
merged.reasoning: Confirmed the ExtendDeadlineCard is shown whenever status is collecting or answering (catchup-home-shell.tsx:110-121), which includes a DORMANT Round (status stays 'collecting' after its window closed with zero questions and the one auto-extension is spent; planNextAction returns {none}). extendPhasePatch (catchups.ts:490-492) for collecting computes from = ms(questionsCloseAt) (the long-past deadline), new = addDays(from, days). extendDeadline's CAS (actions.ts:1224-1231) matches on the stale questionsCloseAt and applies, returning success with phase:'questions'. merged.title: submitPrompt's cap-check comment overstates the transaction: two concurrent submissions can both pass the 40 cap and mint duplicate positions
merged.reasoning: Two-part finding, both confirmed. (1) Comment-vs-reality: the transaction at actions.ts:894-921 is a plain prisma.$transaction (no isolationLevel => READ COMMITTED) that aggregates _count/_max then inserts; under READ COMMITTED two concurrent submissions each read the same committed snapshot (neither sees the other's uncommitted insert), so both pass `_count >= 40` and both insert at position _max+1. The comment at :890-893 ('inside the same transaction as the cap check so two questions arriving together cannot both see room for the last slot') overstates a serialization a plain transaction does not provide; there is no unique on (editionId, position) — TRAPS.md documents it was deliberately NOT added because it would break reorder. So the 40 cap can overshoot to 41 and two prompts can share a position. (2) The duplicate position is tolerated by the createdAt tiebreak on the round reader (round/[editionId]/page.tsx:250) and answer page, but NOT on the home console: loadHome's freshLatest prompts query has no orderBy (page.tsx:262-269) and the JS sort compares position only ([catchupId]/page.tsx:331), so tied rows can shuffle between renders because the DB return order is unstable — the exact symptom Lows 27/34/57 fixed on the other two surfaces. Overshoot harmless (runaway ceiling), shuffle cosmetic, hence Low.
merged.repro: Postgres semantics: no SERIALIZABLE/FOR UPDATE in the transaction, no unique on position, so a two-connection interleave (aggregate/aggregate/insert/insert) yields two rows at the same position and count 41. Render shuffle: a Round with two same-position prompts re-rendered on the home console can show them in swapped order because the prompts query lacks orderBy and the JS sort is position-only.
merged.fix: Give the home console query the same total order the other surfaces have (orderBy [{ position:'asc' }, { createdAt:'asc' }] and/or add createdAt to the JS tiebreak at [catchupId]/page.tsx:331). Correct the submitPrompt comment to state the cap is a best-effort ceiling under READ COMMITTED, not a serialized guarantee (an occasional 41/duplicate-position is tolerated by the tiebreaks).

merged.title: submitEntry (catch-up answer autosave) has no lost-update guard: a stale device silently overwrites a newer answer, and the clear-to-withdraw path can delete or resurrect content under out-of-order saves
merged.reasoning: submitEntry (actions.ts:1398-1416) is an unconditional upsert keyed [promptId, authorId] with no version precondition; the update branch writes the whole body/images field values the request carried. The precedent is real: editPost got exactly this guard in M66 (feed/actions.ts:583-609 - a baseUpdatedAt CAS via updateMany where updatedAt=base, else 'This letter has changed somewhere else'), and its comment names the identical laptop+phone autosave scenario. CatchupEntry has 'updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt' (schema confirmed), so the same token approach is available. So a member editing their own answer on two devices: device A saves paragraphs, device B (stale) blurs and its old body silently overwrites A, both showing saved. The mechanism (no version token) is code-verified. Downgraded from Medium to Low: it needs the same user editing concurrently on two devices and only risks that member's own draft; the atomic-upsert path does not help because a lost update is last-writer-wins on the field regardless. The secondary 'resurrection under out-of-order clears' claim (via the delete-on-empty at 1432-1436) is plausible but more speculative; the core lost-update is the solid part.
merged.repro: Open the same answer in two browser profiles; type and let it save a paragraph in A; in B (still showing the old text) change one character and blur; reload -> A's paragraph is gone with no warning. Letters, the M66 surface, instead answer 'This letter has changed somewhere else.'

merged.gate: An integration test simulating a stale second write to the same [promptId, authorId], asserting the newer content is not clobbered.

merged.title: submitPrompt's cap-and-position transaction claims a concurrency guarantee READ COMMITTED does not give: two simultaneous submits can both pass the cap and take the same position
merged.reasoning: prisma.ts passes no isolationLevel (client construction lines 43-60), so $transaction runs Postgres default READ COMMITTED. submitPrompt's transaction (actions.ts:894-921) runs an aggregate (max position, count) then a create; the comment (actions.ts:889-890) claims 'inside the same transaction as the cap check so two questions arriving together cannot both see room for the last slot'. Under READ COMMITTED an aggregate takes no row locks and neither transaction sees the other's uncommitted insert, so both can read count<MAX and the same _max and both insert - the transaction gives atomicity, not mutual exclusion. The comment overstates the guarantee, which the brief treats as a real finding (comment-vs-code drift). The concrete outcome is benign: the 40-cap is a runaway guard a real group never reaches (actions.ts:88-92), and duplicate positions are deliberately tolerated (no @@unique per TRAPS) and resolved by the [{position asc},{createdAt asc}] render tie-break (page.tsx:100, answer/page.tsx:211). So this is confirmed as the drift, not as a member-visible malfunction.
merged.repro: Code trace: no isolationLevel (prisma.ts), no FOR UPDATE, no unique on (editionId, position). Two Promise.all submitPrompt calls at an edition holding MAX-1 accepted prompts read count=MAX+1 and duplicated position values. The isolation-level reasoning alone settles the mechanism.
merged.fix: Correct the comment so it no longer claims mutual exclusion (the small overshoot and shared position are benign and already handled by the render tie-break); OR, only if the ceiling must be exact, wrap in SERIALIZABLE with a P2034 retry or anchor on SELECT ... FOR UPDATE.
merged.gate: None needed for the comment fix; if hardened, a concurrency test that two same-instant submits at MAX-1 do not both land.

merged.title: setReminderPref and submitEntry use bare upserts on @@unique keys without the P2002 retry the codebase's own rule requires, so a double-tap first-write yields a false 'Something went wrong'
merged.reasoning: setReminderPref (actions.ts:1977-1981) and submitEntry (actions.ts:1398) use a bare prisma.*.upsert on a compound @@unique instead of the upsertCatchupPref helper (actions.ts:1605-1620), whose docblock asserts 'upsert is a read-then-write inside Postgres' that races P2002 on concurrent first-writes. But the repo contradicts itself: joinCatchupByToken (actions.ts:594-600) deliberately uses upsert precisely because 'two taps ... must not throw on the (groupId, userId) unique' - which only holds if Prisma compiles the upsert to an atomic INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, in which case P2002 is never raised and neither the helper nor these two writers need a retry. All three are the same shape (where = compound unique that also appears in create, no nested writes), which is exactly the shape Prisma's native Postgres upsert applies to. The two comments cannot both be right, and which is correct is decided by the emitted SQL, which I cannot inspect statically. Per the brief's 'check whether the DB already prevents the bad outcome atomically', this defaults to a runtime check rather than a hopeful CONFIRMED. Worst-case consequence is Low: a spurious 'Something went wrong' on a rare concurrent first-write while the row actually saved.
merged.repro: Runtime check: enable Prisma query logging (log:['query']) and call setReminderPref with no existing pref row. If it emits INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ("catchupId","userId") DO UPDATE -> atomic, P2002 impossible -> REFUTE (no bug; upsertCatchupPref's retry is dead code and joinCatchupByToken's comment is the correct model). If it emits a SELECT then a conditional INSERT/UPDATE -> emulated, races under concurrency -> CONFIRM Low. The same SQL path governs upsertCatchupPref, joinCatchupByToken and submitEntry, so the whole class stands or falls together.

merged.title: advanceEdition swallows engine failures with console.error only, bypassing the M09 Sentry reporter
merged.reasoning: advanceEdition's catch (catchups.ts:1087-1090) does only console.error('[catchups] advanceEdition failed', err); it never calls the file's own report()/reportSwallowed helper (catchups.ts:71-77). Because advanceEdition never re-throws, the reportSwallowed calls in advanceDueCatchups (catchups.ts:1200) and openNextRoundIfDue's wrapper (catchups.ts:1190) cannot see a per-edition failure - round-OPENING failures are reported, round-ADVANCING failures are not, so the M09 fix is half-applied. report-error.ts's own docblock states the exact failure mode and there is no captureConsole integration (the whole reportSwallowed mechanism exists because console.error on Vercel does not reach Sentry). So a repeatable error inside applyEditionAction (a notify create throwing inside the shared transaction at 960-1001, a constraint violation, a 20s query timeout) is reduced to a Vercel log line: the edition stops advancing on every page view and every nightly tick, /api/catchups/tick still returns {ok:true} 200 (route.ts:31-32), and Sentry stays silent. advanceEdition is also called directly from loadFreshEdition and both catchup pages, so the blind spot is broad; only the admin worklist stuckCatchups count surfaces it. merged.repro: Code trace confirms advanceEdition's catch is console-only and that advanceDueCatchups' report() is unreachable for errors thrown inside advanceEdition. Live: make notifyReminder throw in a dev session with SENTRY_DEV=1 -> no Sentry event, the edition stops advancing, the tick still returns 200.
merged.fix: In advanceEdition's catch, replace console.error with `await report("catchups", err, { step: "advanceEdition", editionId: edition.id })` (report() already exists in this file), keeping the swallow but adding the Sentry report, matching advanceDueCatchups and openNextRoundIfDue.
merged.gate: A source-level assertion/test that advanceEdition's catch routes through reportSwallowed, not a bare console.error (same shape as security-regressions pins).

merged.title: Removing a catch-up photo while another photo is uploading resurrects the removed one (stale images closure)
merged.reasoning: handleFiles (photo-attachments.tsx:43-87) closes over the `images` prop captured at invocation and, on upload completion, calls onChange([...images, ...data.urls]) (line 81). The per-photo Remove button (line 109-116, onClick onChange(images.filter(...))) has no disabled state during an upload - only the Add tile is disabled (`disabled: uploading`, line 127). So with photo A attached, starting an upload of B and removing A during the flight updates the parent's state, but the in-flight handleFiles still holds the stale `images` (with A); when B lands it spreads [A, ...B], resurrecting A. The component's own header says the parent (AnswerCard) owns the autosave and only passes the url array back, so the parent then persists the resurrected list via submitEntry, and the server row re-includes the removed photo. Genuine stale-closure-over-controlled-prop; window is the upload duration (meaningful on a slow phone with a large photo). Low: needs a removal during an in-flight upload.
merged.repro: On an answer with one photo, throttle uploads, add a second photo, then remove the first while 'Adding...' shows; when the upload finishes both photos are present again and the parent autosaves the two-photo list.
merged.fix: In the post-upload onChange, recompute from the freshest prop via a ref (or use a functional updater), rather than the captured `images`; or disable the Remove buttons while `uploading`.
merged.gate: A component test that removing a photo during an in-flight upload does not resurrect it on completion.

merged.title: No reference counting on post image bytes: the same owned URL attached to two rows lets deleting one purge the other's images
merged.reasoning: deletePostWithImages (feed/actions.ts:70-83) queues EVERY parsed url of the deleted post into PendingImagePurge and drains it (deletes the R2 object) with no check whether another Post row references that url. ownedUploadUrls (upload-ownership.ts:31-40) only enforces own-prefix + minted; it does NOT reject a url already stored on another of the caller's posts. merged.title: reportPost double-file TOCTOU: the pending-report dedup is check-then-insert with no unique backstop, unlike reportUser
merged.reasoning: reportPost (report-action.ts:114-160) dedups pending post-reports with a findFirst then create, with NO unique index (deliberately, M29 comment :97-113, because of legacy duplicate rows) AND no P2002 catch — unlike reportUser, which catches P2002 on its @@unique (:219-227) and whose comment concedes 'the findFirst is a fast path, not the guarantee.' Two concurrent submissions of the same (reporter, post) both pass the findFirst under READ COMMITTED, both create Report rows, both call openReportThread (two AdminThreads) and both notifyAdmins — the exact 'one complaint looks like a pattern' effect M29 set out to stop, surviving only in the concurrent case. Rate limits are per-window counters that two concurrent requests can both pass, so they do not serialize this. Admin-facing moderation noise, needs a simultaneous double-submit, hence Low.

merged.title: createPost skips the verified-member gate for any submission carrying saveAsDraft=true, so an unverified account can publish a plain post to the whole feed

But :203 `const isDraft = parsed.data.kind === 'letter' && parsed.data.saveAsDraft === true`, and :261 stores `status: isDraft ? 'draft' : 'published'`. postSchema allows saveAsDraft on any kind (validators.ts:215 kind optional, :245 saveAsDraft optional). So a crafted createPost with saveAsDraft='true' and NO kind field: savingDraft=true (gate skipped), kind defaults to 'post' (:251/:247), isDraft=false, status='published'. requireVerifiedMember (member-gate.ts:59-60) is the ONLY enforcement of emailConfirmed + verifyState==='verified'; nothing between :117 and the create at :247 re-checks. AUTHOR_IN_GOOD_STANDING (posts.ts) filters only isBlocked, not verifyState, so the post renders in every feed. A Stage 0 account (email never confirmed, valid session per the trust model) publishes text to the whole community. Server actions are public HTTP endpoints, so the composer-bypass the comment at :103 claims 'cannot' be bypassed, is.

Expect {success:true, isDraft:false} and the post visible on /feed from a second account. Pure trace: the two quoted conditions (:113 vs :203) are the whole mechanism.

merged.gate: A security-regression test that an unverified/unconfirmed session cannot createPost a published row via saveAsDraft with a non-letter kind.

merged.title: Back/forward navigation restores stale like/love state on letters/[id] and collection/[id], and one tap then silently inverts the member's real state
merged.reasoning: Three verified facts compose. (1) toggleLike (feed/actions.ts:697-703) and togglePhotoLove (collection/actions.ts:559-585) deliberately call NO revalidatePath (heart scroll-jump fix), so the client Router Cache entry for the server-rendered detail page (letters/[id], collection/[id]) is never purged. (2) Next 16 reuses the cached RSC payload on browser back/forward (glossary/staleTimes docs cited). (3) LetterEngagement.handleLike (letter-engagement.tsx:40-50) and PhotoLoveButton.handle (photo-love-button.tsx:24-40) seed useState from server props and, on tap, set only the optimistic next value — they IGNORE the returned {liked/loved:false}, so the inversion is never reconciled. Navigating away and pressing Back re-mounts the detail component from the pre-like payload (heart empty, old count); the client like-state is gone because it never touched the payload. Tapping the stale-empty heart runs the blind delete-first toggle, which DELETES the existing like (returns liked:false), while the UI shows liked/count+1 — UI and DB disagree, and the member's real like is silently lost until a fresh render. Catch-up entries are immune because toggleEntryLove revalidates the round path — the in-repo contrast that confirms this is the omission. Both concrete code defects (no revalidate + ignore returned value) are certain; the trigger is documented Next behavior.
merged.repro: Open a letter, like it, click 'All letters', press browser Back -> heart is empty. Tap it, hard-reload -> heart empty and the Like row is gone (server unliked). Same on collection/[id] via PhotoLoveButton.
merged.fix: Have handleLike/handle adopt result.liked/result.loved (and reconcile the count) from the action response instead of trusting the optimistic value; or revalidate the detail path only (detail pages have no feed-style scroll-jump exposure).
merged.gate: Test/interaction asserting the heart state after back/forward matches the DB, and that the handler adopts the server-returned liked/loved.

merged.title: Letter autosave timer races an explicit Publish/Save: its in-flight guard reads stale closure state
merged.reasoning: The autosave timer callback (create-post-form.tsx:313-318) guards with `if (submitting || savingDraft) return;`, reading those from the closure of the effect that armed it, whose deps are [content, title, images, postId] (:367, eslint-disabled). setSubmitting(true) inside handleSubmit re-renders but does NOT re-run that effect (submitting is not a dep), so the already-armed timer's closure still sees submitting=false and proceeds. handleSubmit (:636-643) only awaits an autosave that has already STARTED (autosaveRunRef) and never clears autosaveTimer.current. So a timer armed by a keystroke within 2.5s of a Publish click fires mid-publish and issues a second editPost carrying baseUpdatedAtRef; if it fires while handleSubmit's own editPost is still in flight both writes carry the same base, and editPost's updateMany precondition (:596-606, where updatedAt=base) makes exactly one return 'This letter has changed somewhere else.' For Publish that error aborts the publish (editResult.error branch at :687 skips publishDraft); for Save-as-draft it surfaces as a spurious failure toast. Most likely under a slow connection (publish outlives the 2.5s timer) or a click at ~2.5s. The submittingRef.current set synchronously at :639 is exactly the flag the timer should read and does not.
merged.repro: Resumed draft at /letters/[id]/edit, network throttled: type a character, click 'Publish letter' within ~1.5s; two editPost POSTs race, one returns the 'changed somewhere else' error, shown as a failure toast during (or as an abort of) a successful publish. Pure trace: deps [:367] exclude submitting; handleSubmit never clears autosaveTimer.current.
merged.fix: Have the timer guard read submittingRef.current, and/or have handleSubmit clearTimeout(autosaveTimer.current) before awaiting autosaveRunRef.
merged.gate: Test that a Publish/Save cancels or excludes any pending autosave so only one versioned editPost is in flight.

merged.title: Autosave never persists an audience-only change and can save a stale cityScope: audienceCity is missing from the autosave effect's deps
merged.reasoning: The autosave effect deps are [content, title, images, postId] (create-post-form.tsx:367) and omit audienceCity, which runAutosave sends unconditionally via `fd.set('cityScope', audienceCity ?? '')` (:328) from the effect closure. The audience picker IS present on the resumed-draft desk: letters/[id]/edit/page.tsx passes userPlaces={cities} and initialCityScope (:61,:66) through to the composer, and audienceOptions = userPlaces (:181) renders the picker (:1088-1131) for any member with cities. So (a) picking or clearing an audience with no subsequent typing never re-runs the effect, never arms a timer, and is never autosaved — the desk keeps saying 'Saved' while the choice is unsaved, and abandoning the tab loses it (the B-048 scenario returns); (b) a timer armed by an earlier keystroke fires with the stale closure audienceCity and writes the OLD scope. Only an explicit Publish/Save (handleSubmit reads current state at :662) persists the fresh value.
merged.repro: Open a resumed draft (member has >=1 city), wait for 'Saved', change the 'Show to' chip only, wait 5s — no autosave request fires (network panel) — close the tab, reopen: audience is back to its previous value.
merged.fix: Add audienceCity to the autosave effect deps (and its equivalent to the localStorage belt) so an audience change schedules an autosave and the timer closure captures the current value.
merged.gate: Test that changing the audience alone triggers an autosave carrying the new cityScope.

merged.title: Letters desk loses everything typed since the last 2.5s idle pause on navigate/close: no flush on unmount, no beforeunload/pagehide, and resumed drafts have no local belt except on save failure
merged.reasoning: Both persistence paths are idle-debounced and neither flushes on teardown. The resumed-draft autosave (create-post-form.tsx:301-367) and the fresh-letter localStorage belt (:263-267) fire only after 2.5s of idle, each timer restarts on every keystroke, and each effect cleanup (:363-365 and :266) clearTimeout's the pending write on unmount WITHOUT executing it. There is no beforeunload/pagehide/visibilitychange flush anywhere in src (grep: only motion.tsx and lab/_kit.tsx use visibilitychange, neither for the composer). For a resumed draft writeLocalDraft runs ONLY in runAutosave's failure branch (:354), so during successful typing nothing but React state holds the delta. So writing fluently (keystrokes <2.5s apart) and then clicking 'All letters', Back, or closing the tab discards every word since the last >=2.5s pause silently, while the chrome still shows 'Saved' — the exact B-043 'crash net' promise ('a close or a crash during an outage does not take them') violated during active composition.
merged.repro: Throwaway draft: type a sentence continuously (no 2.5s pause), immediately click 'All letters' (or close the tab), reopen -> the sentence is absent and localStorage has no rv:letter-draft entry for it. Fix-shape: flush in the effect cleanup and add a pagehide handler calling writeLocalDraft synchronously.
merged.fix: Flush the pending write in the effect cleanup and add a pagehide/visibilitychange('hidden') handler that persists synchronously (autosave for resumed drafts, localStorage belt for fresh ones).
merged.gate: Test/interaction asserting a mid-burst navigate-away persists the unsaved text.

merged.title: Comment hearts, letter heart/bookmark, and catch-up entry hearts have no in-flight guard: a double-tap desyncs the heart from the database
merged.reasoning: Three heart handlers lack the in-flight guard that post-card.tsx:156-176 (likeBusy) and photo-love-button.tsx:22 (busy) carry: CommentItem.handleLike (comments-section.tsx:581-591), LetterEngagement.handleLike/handleBookmark (letter-engagement.tsx:40-60), and EntryLoveButton.handleToggle (entry-love-button.tsx:31-41, whose own header comment names LetterEngagement as its model). None sets a busy ref or disables, so a fast double-tap fires two concurrent toggle actions. Server-side each toggle is idempotent (delete-first, P2002-tolerant) so nothing throws, but two interleaved calls settle order-nondeterministically: the DB can land on liked while the client's net optimistic flip shows unliked (or vice versa), and since neither call errors the handler never reconciles — the heart reads wrong until a fresh render, and a stray like notification may be minted. Confirmed as a real missing guard against the two guarded siblings; downgraded to Low because the desync is transient/self-healing and needs a deliberate double-tap, no data loss or crash.
merged.repro: Slow-3G, double-tap a comment heart, reload -> heart/count differs from what was shown pre-reload. Code-diff: post-card/photo-love carry the busy ref; the three cited handlers do not.
merged.fix: Add the same likeBusy/busy ref (early-return while in flight) to the three handlers.
merged.gate: Test asserting a second toggle while one is in flight is a no-op.

merged.title: Feed and profile 'Load more' have no synchronous re-entry guard and no id-dedupe: a double-tap appends the same page twice
merged.reasoning: PostFeed.handleLoadMore (post-feed.tsx:170-195) and ProfileAuthorFeed.handleLoadMore (profile-author-feed.tsx:78-94) rely solely on disabled={loadingMore} set via setState, with no synchronous re-entry ref and no id-dedupe on append (`setPosts(prev => [...prev, ...data.posts])`, :187/:86). The codebase itself records (M35, and its own siblings) that disabled 'only takes effect on the next render' — comments-section guards its pager with loadingMoreRef (:95,:180-198) and dedupes via mergeComments (:138-143); directory-client dedupes by id. Two activations before the re-render (held Enter/key-repeat on the focused button, a janky double-tap) read the same cursor state, fetch the identical page, and append it twice: duplicate posts with duplicate React keys (key={post.id}) feeding auto-animate. The generation check (:178-182) only rejects cross-query staleness, not same-query duplicates. Real gap versus the deduping siblings; Low because the double-activation window is narrow (must beat the commit) and the duplicate cards clear on refresh/filter change.
merged.repro: Throttle /feed with 10+ posts, rapidly double-activate 'Load more' (Enter twice on the focused button) -> duplicated posts and the React duplicate-key console error. Fix is the loadingMoreRef + seen-set that comments-section already carries.
merged.fix: Add a synchronous loadingMoreRef guard and dedupe the appended page by id (as comments-section/directory-client do) in both PostFeed and ProfileAuthorFeed.
merged.gate: Test that a second Load-more activation while one is in flight neither refetches nor appends duplicates.

merged.title: Composer preview object URLs are never revoked on successful post or unmount
merged.reasoning: Asymmetric object-URL lifecycle. create-post-form.tsx:606 creates a preview via URL.createObjectURL(original) for each fresh upload; removeImage (:630-633) is the ONLY revoker. On a successful post the success branch sets setPreviews([]) (:725) without revoking, and there is no unmount cleanup revoking previews, so each posted photo's blob URL stays registered for the SPA session (and the initialImages entries at :144 are R2 URLs, not blobs, so only the fresh-upload blobs leak). Confirmed real leak; Low as the finder notes — file-backed blob URLs pin disk-backed handles/bookkeeping rather than heap, so the cost is handle lifetime in a long-lived session, not OOM.
merged.repro: Code trace: createObjectURL at :606, revoke only in removeImage; the success reset at :718-731 and component teardown both skip revocation. Optional: chrome://blob-internals shows the entries persist after posting three photos and navigating within the SPA.
merged.fix: Revoke the fresh-upload object URLs on successful post (before setPreviews([])) and in an unmount cleanup; leave R2-URL previews (initialImages) alone.
merged.gate: A lint/review note or test that every createObjectURL in the composer is paired with a revoke on discard/unmount.

merged.title: Letter page's raw isHidden check defeats the pinned author-exemption on hidden posts
merged.reasoning: letters/[id]/page.tsx:67 runs `if (!letter || letter.kind !== 'letter' || letter.isHidden) notFound();` BEFORE canViewPost at :88, so the raw Post.isHidden column short-circuits the page. decidePostVisibility (post-visibility-rule.ts:190 author exemption, above the hidden check at :202) — the settled owner decision recorded in bugs.md ('the post visibility rule's author exemption sits ABOVE the hidden check... a test pins it') — is therefore unreachable on this surface: the author of an admin-hidden LETTER gets a 404 on their own letter, defeating the one way they could respond to the moderation. The comment directly beneath (:69-86) argues for exactly the 'one rule, canViewPost already exempts the author' behavior the line above it breaks. Internal inconsistency confirms the drift: generateMetadata in the same file (:40-41) gates with canViewPost only, so the author of a hidden letter gets the real title in the tab while the body 404s. canViewPost still returns not-ok (hidden) for non-author non-admins, so removing the raw check does not leak. Low: needs prior admin moderation and only affects the author, mild consequence, but a genuine settled-decision breach and comment-vs-code drift.
merged.repro: Publish a letter, admin-hide it, open /letters/<id> as the author -> hoopoe 404 (with the correct letter title in the browser tab, from generateMetadata). A hidden feed post's author-exemption path (canViewPost) is not pre-empted this way. Trace: :67 raw isHidden precedes :88 canViewPost.

merged.gate: Test that a hidden letter 404s for a non-author but renders for its author, mirroring the decidePostVisibility author-exemption test.

merged.title: reportPost skips the post-visibility rule every other post interaction enforces, leaking existence and author name of drafts/hidden/scoped posts
merged.reasoning: report-action.ts:91-95 fetches the post with a bare findUnique (id + author.name) and never calls canViewPost/decidePostVisibility, unlike the six interaction paths the post-visibility.ts header (lines 19-28) says were fixed for H3 (createComment/toggleLike/toggleBookmark/votePoll/toggleCommentLike/loadComments each gate on canViewPost — feed/actions.ts:635,713,757,1316,1398). So a verified member holding an id they cannot see can file a report; the 'That post is already gone' branch (line 95) is an existence oracle, and on success openReportThread writes subject `A post by ${post.author.name}` (line 140) plus a reporter notification (line 57), disclosing the author's name. Real read-path/write-path enforcement mismatch. Downgraded to Low: createPost refuses groupId and there are zero group posts (feed/actions.ts:170-181), so the private-group surface H3 mainly protected does not exist; for city/batch-scoped posts the author is generally already known to anyone holding the id; and cuid ids are not enumerable.

merged.fix: Call canViewPost(postId, session.user) after fetching (or in place of the bare findUnique) and return POST_NOT_VISIBLE when !ok, mirroring toggleLike/createComment; keep the author-name writes below that gate.
merged.gate: Extend the post-visibility / security-regressions tests with a case asserting reportPost on a non-visible post returns the not-visible error.

merged.title: Hidden letters 404 for the admin and the author because letters/[id] checks isHidden before canViewPost, defeating both documented exemptions
merged.reasoning: letters/[id]/page.tsx:67 `if (!letter || letter.kind !== 'letter' || letter.isHidden) notFound();` runs BEFORE canViewPost at line 88. decidePostVisibility admits admin (post-visibility-rule.ts:180) and author (line 190) ABOVE the isHidden refusal (line 202), and both bugs.md 'Settled' and the rule comment (lines 195-199) promise a moderator following an /admin/content link lands on the post and an author can reach a hidden post to respond to moderation. admin-content-query.ts:79 sets a letter href to `/letters/${p.id}` and includes hidden rows when includeHidden (line 36), so the moderation list's own Open on a hidden letter 404s. A hidden (admin-removed, status still published) letter is filtered from loadPosts (feed/actions.ts:1049) and the letters index (letters/page.tsx:70), so its author has no other route; line 67 defeats the documented exemption whose ONLY page surface is this one (plain posts have no reading page). This is the page overriding the rule, distinct from the settled note which only affirms the rule.

merged.title: Feed keyset pagination silently ends when the cursor post is deleted between pages
merged.reasoning: loadPosts recent path uses `cursor:{id:keysetCursor}, skip:1` (feed/actions.ts:1114) and posts are hard-deleted (deletePostWithImages -> tx.post.delete, line 78), so a boundary cursor id can vanish between pages. The finding hinges entirely on Prisma 7 + @prisma/adapter-pg returning an EMPTY result (rather than a full first page or an error) when the cursor row no longer exists — a runtime behavior that cannot be settled from source. If true, hasMore=false/nextCursor=null ends infinite scroll early, but a full reload re-seeds a fresh cursor and recovers, so Medium at most. Same pattern in loadComments roots (line 1414), though comments are soft-deleted except account-purge.

Result [] confirms the bug; a full first page or a thrown error refutes/reshapes it. Then end-to-end: create >21 posts, load page 1, hard-delete the returned nextCursor post, call loadPosts with that cursor and observe an empty page while older posts exist.

merged.title: reportPost's report -> thread -> notify chain has no transaction; a mid-chain failure leaves a pending Report whose retry answers success without ever creating the thread
merged.reasoning: reportPost runs report.create (line 130), openReportThread (adminThread + notification, lines 37-60), notifyAdmins (148) and writeAudit (153) as four separate awaits with no $transaction. If openReportThread throws after report.create commits (pool timeout/dropped connection), a pending Report exists with no thread and no admin notification; the first call surfaces an error, and every retry hits the openAlready dedupe (lines 114-128), which finds the pending Report and returns {success:true, alreadyReported:true} — it even selects thread.id (line 121) and ignores that it is null. reportUser has the same shape via the P2002 catch (lines 219-227). Confirmed check-then-act over a multi-write chain. Low: the Report still reaches /admin/reports (moderation not lost); only the reporter's follow-up thread and the admin ping are missing, and only after a rare mid-chain failure.
merged.repro: Code trace above. Live confirmation: query Report rows with status 'pending' whose thread relation is null — any hit is this already realized.
merged.fix: Create the Report and its AdminThread (+ first message) inside one $transaction so the dedupe's Report row implies the thread exists; or in the openAlready branch, when thread is null, re-drive openReportThread before returning.
merged.gate: A test that a report whose thread-creation fails, on retry, ends with both a Report and an AdminThread (or a monitoring query for pending reports lacking a thread).

merged.reasoning: letters/page.tsx:64-77 builds the index where with batchScopeWhere(userBatch) and `AND:[cityScopeWhere(viewerCities)]` and NO `OR authorId` arm, unlike loadPosts which spells the author exemption out twice (feed/actions.ts:1044 and 1075) for M30. Confirmed list-vs-list inconsistency. Low: only the author's own view of one of three surfaces, needs a post-hoc profile change, no data loss.

merged.fix: Add `OR:[cityScopeWhere(viewerCities), {authorId: session.user.id}]` (and the batch equivalent) to the letters index where, mirroring loadPosts.
merged.gate: A test that a city-scoped letter stays in its author's /letters after the author's city list no longer matches.

Confirmed over-broad dedupe / silent write-drop. Low: needs two genuinely distinct posts with identical short content within 10s.

merged.reasoning: CommentItem.handleLike (comments-section.tsx:581-591) has no in-flight guard, unlike PostCard.handleLike/handleBookmark which key off likeBusy/bookmarkBusy refs (post-card.tsx:156-176,197-217). Confirmed. Low: needs a fast double-tap on a slow connection.

merged.title: Long posts are split at a hard 300-char boundary: formatting or a mention spanning it renders as raw markers, an emoji can split into lone surrogates, and the remainder starts on a new line mid-word
merged.reasoning:
For non-letter posts >300 chars, post-card.tsx:131-134 splits leadText=content.slice(0,300)/restText=content.slice(300) and renders each through renderRichText separately (lines 350,365). renderRichText's emphasis rules require both delimiters in one string (utils.ts:605-642) and mentions are matched whole (utils.ts:651-654), so a **bold**, @[Name](id) mention, or surrogate/ZWJ emoji straddling index 300 renders as literal markers / U+FFFD, and because restText is a second block

, an expanded post resumes on a new line mid-word. Confirmed boundary-split rendering (letters render whole via /letters/[id], unaffected). Low: cosmetic, needs formatting/emoji exactly at char 300 of a long plain post.
merged.repro: Post ~350 chars with a bold span from ~char 290-310 -> literal ** visible collapsed and expanded, and the remainder breaks the line mid-word.
merged.fix: Render renderRichText(content) once and truncate the RENDERED output, or split on a safe boundary (Intl.Segmenter / word boundary, never inside a markdown token) so both halves keep one rendered string.
merged.gate: A unit test that a bold/mention/emoji spanning the truncation index renders identically to the un-split render.

Practical exposure is small: no admin surface lists draft ids (admin-content applies PUBLISHED_ONLY, admin-content-query.ts:49), so an admin needs the id out-of-band. Confirmed as the comment/code drift the task asks me to flag, not an imagined new leak.

merged.gate: A post-visibility-rule unit test pinning the chosen behavior for (admin viewer, draft post).

merged.title: Report dialog lets details reach 500 chars, then prefixes the reason so the combined string exceeds the server's 500 cap and the report is refused opaquely
merged.reasoning: report-dialog.tsx caps details at maxLength=500 (line 97) then builds fullReason = `${reason}: ${details}` (line 44), prepending 6-23 chars; report-action.ts:87 refuses trimmed.length>500 with the generic 'Please provide a valid reason.' Low: needs ~495+ chars in an optional field.

merged.gate: A test that a 500-char details plus any reason submits successfully.

'new'}` (create-post-form.tsx:239) carries no user id, and the restore effect (lines 270-289) loads it on any /letters/new mount (defaultLetter && !initialContent). merged.title: No length cap on the feed search term: loadPosts LIKE-scans title, content and author name with an unbounded pattern
merged.reasoning: loadPosts feeds opts.search through escapeLike (which only neutralizes LIKE wildcards, so no % injection) into three `contains` clauses (feed/actions.ts:1029-1036) with no length cap, and loadPosts has no rate limit (reads unmetered). The header search-pill has no maxLength (search-pill.tsx:167-173) and posts to /feed?q= -> post-feed -> loadPosts (post-feed.tsx:108-116); the action is directly callable, so pattern length is caller-chosen. A pattern near the text length turns each %pattern% row match into ~O(text^2) work (naive substring match, no wildcard early-out), so a ~20KB q makes each ~20k-char letter row hundreds of millions of comparisons; query_timeout (20s, prisma.ts) bounds one query but ties a pool connection (max 5) for up to 20s, repeatable. Confirmed missing input cap with a nameable stability cost. Low: crafted-call DoS bounded by query_timeout, not a normal member path. Note: the finding's premise that directory people-search was capped at FULL_NAME_MAX is inaccurate — directory/where.ts:41-48 is also uncapped — so a fix should cover both search paths.
merged.repro: Code trace above; optional live = one timed loadPosts({search:<~20KB string>}) call and read the wall-clock against the 20s query_timeout.
merged.fix: Clamp opts.search (e.g. .slice(0,100)) in loadPosts before escapeLike, and the same in buildDirectoryWhere.
merged.gate: A unit test that loadPosts truncates an over-long search before querying.

merged.title: Replying to a reply notifies the root comment's author, not the person actually replied to, while the UI promises 'Replying to <them>'
merged.reasoning: When replying to a reply the composer sets replyTo.id to the ROOT comment's id but the displayed name to the reply author's (comments-section.tsx:377-384: `id: comment.deleted ? reply.id : comment.id, name: reply.author!.name`), so 'Replying to B' shows while parentId=A is sent. createComment then notifies the (promoted) parentId's author (feed/actions.ts:781-783,843-864) — root author A gets 'replied to your comment' and B (whose reply was tapped and whose name the UI showed) is never notified. Even when reply.id is sent (deleted root branch) the server promotes to A and still notifies A. Confirmed misdirected notification. Low: notification-quality only, no data loss.
merged.repro: A roots, B replies, C taps Reply on B's reply and posts -> Notification rows: one type 'reply' for A, none for B.
merged.fix: Carry the actually-replied-to comment's author and notify them (or notify both the root and the tapped reply author) rather than only the promoted root author.
merged.gate: A test asserting a reply-to-reply notifies the tapped reply's author.

merged.title: A draft's saved city audience silently widens to Everyone if the city was removed from the profile before a save lands
merged.reasoning: editPost applies cityScopeUpdate only for a letter draft (feed/actions.ts:552-566) and folds a city that no longer matches the author's UserPlace to {cityScope:null} (Everyone) — the same stored value as a deliberate 'Everyone' — with no error or signal. The desk autosaves cityScope unconditionally (create-post-form.tsx:328). So if the author removes city X (settings/another tab) while a draft scoped to X is open, the next autosave (fired by a keystroke; audienceCity state and thus the 'X only' chip are unchanged) sends X, editPost resolves it to null, and publishDraft then publishes to everyone. Confirmed silent audience widening. Low: narrow trigger but privacy-relevant. Distinct from C-008 (read narrowing) — this is a write widening.
merged.repro: Save a draft scoped to own city X, remove X in settings in another tab, type one char in the desk, wait for autosave, read the row's cityScope (null) while the chip still says 'X only'.
merged.fix: Distinguish a validation miss from an intentional clear — when a non-empty wanted city fails to match a UserPlace, refuse the save (surface an error / keep the stored value) rather than folding to null.
merged.gate: A test that editPost with a cityScope the author no longer lists does not silently set cityScope to null.

merged.title: Feed post notifications deep-link to /feed#<postId> but nothing implements the scroll; the module comment claims PostFeed does
merged.reasoning: Verified against the actual code. postNotificationLink returns `/feed#${post.id}` for every non-letter post (notification-links.ts:28); the bell navigates with router.push(notif.link) (notification-bell.tsx:235); PostCard renders `<article id={post.id}>` (post-card.tsx:234) but PostFeed fetches posts in a useEffect after mount behind a skeleton (post-feed.tsx:120-160) so the anchor does not exist when the router commits. A repo-wide grep for location.hash/scrollIntoView/getElementById finds NO reader of the fragment in the feed path (only lab landings, house-picker, tour-provider, catchups toc, landing-nav). The repo's OWN lab audit independently states it: src/app/lab/everything/_findings.ts feed-2, 'The feed fetches its posts after mount and nothing reads the URL hash... it silently gives up.' The module comment at notification-links.ts:13-15 ('PostFeed handles the scrolling half of the feed case, once its first page has loaded') is therefore a confirmed comment-vs-code mismatch: PostFeed does no such thing. Severity corrected High->Medium: the navigation still lands on a working feed and a recent post is on the page (just not scrolled/highlighted); only posts older than the first page (20) are truly unreachable. Non-crashing degradation on a common path.
merged.repro: Two accounts: B likes A's 21st-newest post so it falls off page one. A taps the 'B liked your post' notification -> router.push('/feed#<postId>') -> feed renders skeleton then loads 20 posts, none with that id, no hash read -> A lands at feed top, target post absent. Code trace: notification-links.ts:28 -> notification-bell.tsx:235 -> post-feed.tsx:120-160 (no hash consumer) confirmed by grep and _findings.ts feed-2.
merged.fix: Either give a post its own server-rendered route and point postNotificationLink (and Share, see new finding) at it, or have PostFeed read window.location.hash once the first page resolves, fetch the post if it is missing from the page, scroll it into view and ring the card. Separately correct the false comment at notification-links.ts:13-15.
merged.gate: e2e that clicks a like/comment notification and asserts the target article is scrolled into view (expect.poll on geometry); at minimum a unit test pinning the link plus a documented, actually-present scroll mechanism.

merged.title: Closing a thread ('Sorted') unconditionally clears adminUnread, burying a member reply that arrived after the admin loaded the page
merged.reasoning: setThreadStatus (messages/actions.ts:235-238) does a plain `update({ where:{id}, data:{ status, adminUnread:false } })` with no precondition, unlike the conditional updateMany used elsewhere. A member reply committing after the admin's /admin/messages/[id] render sets adminUnread:true + status:open (replyToThread, actions.ts:151-156); a later setThreadStatus('closed') then clears adminUnread, archiving the thread to Sorted with no New chip. Mechanism confirmed. Severity corrected Medium->Low: the finder's 'silently marked seen / nothing resurfaces it' claim is overstated because replyToThread ALSO calls notifyAdmins (actions.ts:159-162), fanning a fresh 'X replied about ...' bell notification to every admin that links straight at the thread. So the reply is not lost, only the thread-queue unread marker is wrong; the bell is the backstop. Real TOCTOU, low consequence.
merged.repro: Admin opens thread (markThreadSeenByAdmin clears adminUnread). Member calls replyToThread -> adminUnread=true, status=open, notifyAdmins fires. Admin, without refresh, clicks Mark sorted -> setThreadStatus('closed') -> row ends status=closed, adminUnread=false while the last AdminMessage is the unreviewed member reply. Verifiable by reading actions.ts:219-243 against 138-162.
merged.fix: Guard the clear the way settleReport guards its transition: only clear adminUnread when lastMessageAt has not advanced past the value the admin's page rendered (pass the rendered lastMessageAt and add it to the updateMany where), or drop adminUnread from setThreadStatus entirely and let the open-page markThreadSeenByAdmin own the flag.
merged.gate: Unit/integration test: setThreadStatus('closed') on a thread whose lastMessageAt moved after render leaves adminUnread=true.

merged.title: A legacy unresolved admin_note can be permanently destroyed by mark-all-read plus the 100-row prune, losing the moderation note's only copy
merged.reasoning: Mechanism fully verified. Legacy notifyAdminNote (git show 4ab894a:src/lib/admin-note.ts) stored the full note ONLY in Notification.message with link `/notice/<notificationId>` and created NO thread; the note materialises into an AdminThread only on a /notice/[id] visit (notice/[id]/page.tsx:54-69). markAllNotificationsRead (notifications/actions.ts:124-127) flips read=true with no type exemption; the first-page prune (notifications/actions.ts:58-60) deletes read rows past position 100 with no type exemption; retention.ts:127-129 deletes notifications older than 365 days regardless of read state. So an unopened legacy admin_note can be destroyed and its only copy lost. Current notifyAdminNote (admin-note.ts:22-35) creates the thread EAGERLY and links to /messages/, so all post-messaging notes are safe. The whole finding therefore hinges on whether any legacy `/notice/%` admin_note rows still exist in the production DB, which I cannot query (read-only, no DB). Severity Medium only if such rows exist; likely lower since the population is bounded to the pre-messaging window and is now ~1 year old.
merged.repro: Runtime: SELECT count(*) FROM "Notification" WHERE type='admin_note' AND link LIKE '/notice/%'. If >0, a rolled-back tx can show the delete: BEGIN; UPDATE read=true on one; run the prune's cutoff+deleteMany; observe the row gone; ROLLBACK. If 0, the finding is moot.
merged.fix: If legacy rows exist: backfill them into AdminThreads once (a one-shot migration mirroring notice/[id] resolution) so the text no longer lives only in Notification.message, OR exempt type IN ('admin_note') from the read-based prune the way unread rows are already exempt.
merged.gate: The migration/exemption plus a test that an admin_note notification is never deleted while its thread does not exist.

merged.title: Bell infinite scroll silently truncates when the cursor row is pruned by a concurrent first-page open (second tab/device)
merged.reasoning: The code shape is real: getNotifications pages with `cursor:{id}, skip:1` (notifications/actions.ts:34) and the prune is skipped on cursor pages (line 44), so a concurrent first-page open from another tab/device runs the prune (deleteMany read rows past position 100, lines 58-60) and could delete a cursor row another session holds. But two things gate it hard. (1) The prune only deletes rows BEYOND position 100, so the held cursor must sit past the 100 newest notifications; reaching that in a max-h-80 dropdown needs 3-5 'load more' fetches, an implausible bell scroll. (2) Every row past position 100 that a session cannot reach because of this is a READ row the prune is deleting anyway, so the only non-trivial loss is unread rows past position 100 (rare, and re-openable since handleOpen refetches page one). The load-bearing claim 'Prisma returns an empty set for a deleted cursor row' is documentation-derived, not verified against this repo. Given the negligible member-visible consequence and the unverified Prisma semantics, this needs a live check rather than a confirm.
merged.repro: Runtime: (a) confirm Prisma 7 returns [] (not a throw, not a resume-after) for `cursor:{id: <deleted>}` against Notification; (b) seed ~130 read notifications, hold a page-2+ cursor beyond position 100 in tab A, open the bell in tab B to fire the prune, then scroll tab A and check whether it ends early while unread rows past 100 remain. If (a) is false or (b) leaves no unread rows stranded, refute.

merged.title: Admin-opened notice threads count against the member's own new-thread budget, which also gates reporting
merged.reasoning: Verified. isThreadRateLimited counts adminThread.count({ where:{ memberId, createdAt: gte } }) with NO kind filter and no notion of author (admin-threads-server.ts:27-33). openAdminNoticeThread writes kind 'notice' rows with memberId = the moderated member (admin-threads-server.ts:94-118), driven by notifyAdminNote on post removal (feed/actions.ts:454), comment removal (feed/actions.ts:941) and Collection photo removal (collection/actions.ts:676), each only when the admin attaches a note. Both member-facing consumers gate on this same count: startThread (messages/actions.ts:84) and reportPost (report-action.ts:82). So an admin who removes 5 of one member's items with notes inside an hour creates 5 notice threads under that member's memberId, and the member is then refused both a new thread ('That's a lot of messages') and any report ('That's a lot of reports') for up to an hour, having sent nothing. MAX_NEW_THREADS_PER_HOUR=5 (admin-threads.ts:25). Real logic bug; Low because it requires 5 admin note-actions on one member within a rolling hour and self-clears.
merged.repro: Trace: admin-threads-server.ts:29-32 (count has no kind filter) + admin-note.ts:24 (openAdminNoticeThread memberId=userId) + messages/actions.ts:84 and report-action.ts:82 (both call isThreadRateLimited(session.user.id)). Live: as admin, remove 5 of member X's posts with notes within an hour; as X, attempt startThread -> refused.
merged.fix: Exclude admin-originated rows from the budget: count only threads the member created, e.g. add `kind: { notIn: ['notice'] }` (or filter on the first message's fromAdmin=false / authorId=memberId) in isThreadRateLimited. Reports (kind 'report') stay counted per audit H5.
merged.gate: Test that N kind='notice' threads under a memberId do not raise isThreadRateLimited for that member.

merged.title: Member /messages list silently caps at 60 threads with no affordance — the same shape as fixed audit B-200 on the admin side
merged.reasoning: Verified. messages/page.tsx:29-47 fetches the member's threads with `take: 60`, orderBy lastMessageAt desc, and no count, no pagination, no 'show older' affordance. This is exactly the shape audit B-200 fixed on the admin side (admin/messages/page.tsx:23-32 comment: 'every thread past position sixty became permanently unreachable... with nothing on the page to say so'); the member page kept the bare take. The only member-facing list of threads is this page, and notifications that deep-link to older threads prune at KEEP=100 (notifications/actions.ts:58-60), so a member past 60 threads whose old notifications have pruned cannot reach the older conversations. Low: reaching 60 distinct threads as one member (own messages + each report + each moderation-note thread) is uncommon but reachable over the life of the site.
merged.repro: Trace: messages/page.tsx:31 (take:60, no escape) vs admin/messages/page.tsx SORTED_PAGE=40 with 'Show N older'. A seeded account with 61 threads returns 60; the 61st is unreachable and nothing on the page indicates it exists.
