merged.fix: Mirror the B-200 fix: keep the cap but add a 'Show older' link (or keyset pagination) and a total count, so no thread is silently unreachable.
merged.gate: Test/assertion that the member messages page exposes threads beyond position 60 via an escape, or renders a total count.

merged.title: deriveSubject/previewOf cut at UTF-16 code-unit offsets, splitting surrogate pairs into U+FFFD mojibake in stored subjects and notification copy
merged.reasoning: Verified. deriveSubject (admin-threads.ts:60-70) cuts with `flat.slice(0,64)` and `cut.slice(0,lastSpace)`; previewOf (admin-threads.ts:73-76) cuts with `flat.slice(0, max-1)`. String.prototype.slice indexes UTF-16 code units, and every astral char (emoji, etc.) is a 2-unit surrogate pair, so a slice at an odd boundary relative to the pairs lands mid-pair and yields a lone surrogate. previewOf is called as previewOf(body,70) in startThread/notifyAdmins -> slice(0,69), an ODD offset: on an all-emoji body (pairs at even boundaries) index 69 splits a pair. The lone surrogate is not encodable as valid UTF-8, so node-postgres' Buffer.from(str,'utf8') substitutes U+FFFD, persisting mojibake in AdminThread.subject (the thread title everywhere) and Notification.message previews. TRAPS.md explicitly names Intl.Segmenter (constructed once at module load) as this codebase's text-cutting instrument (getInitials learned exactly this). Real, persistent, member-visible; Low (cosmetic-with-teeth).
merged.repro: Pure-function check, no DB: run deriveSubject/previewOf logic on a 70-emoji string; previewOf(s,70)=s.slice(0,69) ends in an unpaired high surrogate (charCodeAt in D800-DBFF); Buffer.from(thatString,'utf8') yields a trailing EF BF BD. .trimEnd() in previewOf does not strip surrogates.
merged.fix: Cut on grapheme boundaries using a module-scope Intl.Segmenter (as getInitials does) instead of raw slice in both deriveSubject and previewOf, so no cut lands mid-pair.
merged.gate: Unit test asserting deriveSubject/previewOf never return a string whose final code unit is a lone surrogate, over an emoji-heavy no-space input.

merged.title: Mark-read-on-open clears an unread flag for a message that arrived after the page's message query (both member and admin thread pages)
merged.reasoning: Verified same class as C-053, milliseconds-wide. Member page loads messages via findUnique (messages/[id]/page.tsx:36-64) then clears memberUnread via updateMany (83-86); admin page loads then calls markThreadSeenByAdmin (admin/messages/[id]/page.tsx:93-95). A reply committing between the read and the clear has its just-set flag cleared without being in the rendered page. The `where: memberUnread:true` / `adminUnread:true` guards protect the flag WRITE (B-201) but not this read-then-clear inversion. Self-heals on the next message, and adminReplyToThread creates a member Notification (actions.ts:203-210) / replyToThread fires notifyAdmins, so a bell backstop exists. Real but negligible; Low.
merged.repro: Trace only: no transaction or lastMessageAt condition ties the clear (messages/[id]/page.tsx:83-86) to the message snapshot loaded at 36-64. Interleaving an adminReplyToThread commit between the two statements clears memberUnread for the unshown message.
merged.fix: Fold into the C-053 fix: condition the unread clear on the rendered snapshot, e.g. clear only when no AdminMessage newer than the loaded page's newest exists (or updateMany scoped by lastMessageAt <= rendered value).
merged.gate: Shared with C-053: a test that a message committing after the page's message query is not marked seen.

merged.title: Admin Messages page fetches every open thread unbounded
merged.reasoning: Verified. The open-threads query in admin/messages/page.tsx (the first findMany, lines 75-79, where status not 'closed') has NO take, while the sibling closed-threads query one statement below is capped at SORTED_PAGE=40 with a Show-older escape and a defending comment. AdminThread.status defaults to 'open' (schema.prisma), openAdminNoticeThread never sets status, and nothing auto-closes threads, so every moderation-note ('notice') thread and every unsorted report/message accumulates permanently in the open list, each rendered with an 8-field member join and a last-message subquery. Admin-only degradation that grows over the life of the site. Low: admin-facing, slow-burn, bounded by the 20s query timeout long before it hard-fails.
merged.repro: Trace: admin/messages/page.tsx:75 (no take on the status!=closed findMany) vs 80-85 (take:SORTED_PAGE on the closed one) + schema default status 'open' + no auto-close anywhere. Count grows as SELECT count(*) FROM "AdminThread" WHERE status <> 'closed'.
merged.fix: Cap the open query too (take + a Show-older/paginate escape mirroring the closed section), or auto-close/expire notice threads that need no admin action so they leave the work queue.
merged.gate: Assertion that the open-threads findMany carries a take.

merged.title: Notification pagination silently ends when the cursor row was pruned by another device's bell-open
merged.reasoning: Identical root cause to C-056 from the same angle: getNotifications cursor pagination (notifications/actions.ts:34) can end early when a concurrent first-page open prunes the held cursor row, relying on Prisma's missing-cursor-returns-empty behavior. Same file, same lines, same mechanism, same negligible consequence. Validated canonically under C-056 (NEEDS-LIVE, Low).

merged.title: startThread and replyToThread have no double-submit guard: a double-tap or two-tab send files the same message twice and pages the admins twice
merged.reasoning: Verified. startThread (messages/actions.ts:71-109) and replyToThread (112-168) create an AdminThread/AdminMessage with only hourly rate limits and NO double-submit twin guard; the messages actions file does not import DOUBLE_SUBMIT_MS at all (grep shows only feed/actions.ts and catchups/actions.ts consume it, and double-submit.ts's own comment names 'the feed and Catch-ups' as its consumers). Two concurrent invocations (two tabs/devices, a retried request, or a client whose setState 'sending' guard has not yet bound) both pass the rate limit and file two identical threads/replies, each firing its own notifyAdmins fan-out. Same free-text/no-unique-index shape M35 fixed for posts and comments. Low: duplicates a human cleans up (two admin rows, doubled bell noise, member sees two conversations), no corruption.
merged.repro: Throttle network in dev, double-fire Send on /messages: two AdminThread rows with identical body/createdAt within a second and two admin notifications. Code: messages/actions.ts:88 and :138-140 have no `findFirst`/DOUBLE_SUBMIT_MS twin lookup, unlike feed/actions.ts:223-237.
merged.fix: Add the server twin-window guard to startThread and replyToThread as feed/catchups do (look for the caller's own identical message within DOUBLE_SUBMIT_MS and return the first), and/or a synchronous ref guard in MessageComposer (see C-181).
merged.gate: Test that two identical startThread (and replyToThread) calls within DOUBLE_SUBMIT_MS produce one row.

merged.title: Message composer and Collection contribute dialog keep state-only double-submit guards the M35 audit already ruled insufficient
merged.reasoning: The in-batch (messages) half of C-181 is the same bug as C-128 from the client angle: MessageComposer.handleSend guards only on the `canSend` closure over `sending` state (message-composer.tsx:57-58,90-92), a state-only guard the M35 audit already ruled insufficient because setState binds on the next render, so Cmd/Ctrl+Enter key-repeat plus a Send click can reach startThread/replyToThread twice. Root cause and member-visible outcome (duplicate admin threads/replies) are identical to C-128; the fix (a synchronous submittingRef and/or the server twin guard) resolves both. The second surface C-181 raises, ContributeDialog (contribute-dialog.tsx, Collection), is a different feature outside the Z05-messages batch and should be validated by the Collection batch; it is not evaluated here.

merged.title: chooseBird's header comment describes the abolished re-pick model the code below refuses
merged.reasoning: Verified comment-vs-code drift, exactly the class the audit brief says to confirm. The chooseBird header comment (src/app/(main)/support/actions.ts:206-208) asserts 'Re-picking is allowed indefinitely. The perk is standing, and the write is idempotent, so there is nothing to meter and no state to corrupt by clicking twice.' The code below (actions.ts:236-256) does the opposite: it implements 'One pick per contribution (owner, 2026-08-18)' — birdPickedAt SPENDS the pick (line 243) and a re-pick is refused unless a paid contribution exists with paidAt > birdPickedAt (lines 244-255, returning 'You have already picked your bird. A new contribution opens another pick.'). The inner block carries the 2026-08-18 owner date, so the header is the stale one describing the abolished free-repick model. It absolutely meters and there absolutely is state to corrupt by clicking twice: a member double-clicking the same bird gets the first click spend the grant (line 261 sets birdPickedAt) and the second click error out (line 254). Documentation defect, not behavioral — the code is correct, the comment lies.
merged.repro: Read actions.ts:206-208 (header: 're-picking allowed indefinitely / nothing to meter / no state to corrupt') against actions.ts:243-255 (one-pick-per-contribution gate that meters and errors on a second pick). They state opposite policies in one function; the 2026-08-18 owner date sits on the inner block, so the header predates the change.
merged.fix: Rewrite the header comment (actions.ts:206-208) to describe the shipped one-pick-per-contribution model: a pick is spent on use and regranted only by a paid contribution newer than the last spend. Do not touch the code; the gate is deliberate.
merged.gate: No runtime gate; a reviewer diff-check. Optionally a doc-lint that the header no longer contains 'allowed indefinitely'.

merged.title: Duplicate/out-of-order payment.captured resurrects a refunded contribution to "paid" (and re-grants a bird pick)
merged.reasoning: Confirmed against the code. Webhook captured branch at src/app/api/razorpay/webhook/route.ts:163-164 is updateMany({ where: { id, status: { not: "paid" } }, data: { status: "paid", paidAt: new Date(), failureReason: null, method, razorpayPaymentId } }). 'refunded' and 'disputed' both satisfy status != 'paid', so a re-delivered payment.captured (Razorpay retries any delivery it did not 2xx, plus the dashboard 'resend webhook' button) landing after a refund flips the terminal row back to 'paid' with a FRESH paidAt. Consequences all verified: every money sum filters status='paid' (support/page.tsx:41, actions.ts:226, admin-analytics.ts:280, admin/support/page.tsx:81), so the returned gift re-counts in the public recovery bar and 'Given, all time'; the fresh paidAt > birdPickedAt makes chooseBird's regrant query (actions.ts:244-249) mint a new bird pick; and moved.count===1 fires the 'Your contribution came through' notification (route.ts:191-200) after a refund. The mirror half is also real: the refund/dispute branch (route.ts:230-233) guards status:'paid', so a refund.processed arriving while the row is still 'created' (capture delayed/retrying, browser callback lost) matches nothing, moved.count=0, falls through to 200 at route.ts:248, Razorpay never resends, and a later captured lands the row on 'paid' with the refund unrecorded and no audit line (writeAudit at route.ts:238 is inside moved.count===1). Root cause: the paid-transition predicate excludes only the state it wants to reach, not the terminal reversal states added later in 220ebec (audit M58) without narrowing the WHERE. Downgraded High→Medium: not a normal-member path (needs a refund/dispute plus webhook redelivery/reordering or manual resend), but when it fires the corruption is silent, persistent, and only hand-SQL against the shared production DB can undo it.
merged.repro: Rolled-back txn via scripts/dev/run-sql.mjs: BEGIN; UPDATE "Contribution" SET status='refunded' WHERE id=<test row>; then run the captured branch's exact statement UPDATE "Contribution" SET status='paid', "paidAt"=now() WHERE id=<row> AND status <> 'paid'; SELECT status, "paidAt"; ROLLBACK — the row reads paid with a new paidAt, proving refunded is not terminal. Live: test mode pay, refund, then dashboard 'resend' the payment.captured event and watch the /support recovery bar re-inflate.
merged.fix: Two distinct changes. (1) Resurrection: narrow route.ts:164 from status:{ not:'paid' } to status:{ in:['created','failed'] } so refunded/disputed are terminal (apply the same narrowing to confirmContribution, C-085). (2) Refund-before-capture lost (mirror / C-151): when refund.processed or dispute.created finds the row not-yet-paid, do not silently 200-and-drop — persist the pending reversal so it applies once capture lands, or return a non-2xx so Razorpay redelivers after capture, and write an audit line either way.
merged.gate: New webhook state-machine test (node --test) asserting: a payment.captured cannot move a row out of 'refunded'/'disputed'; and a refund.processed on a 'created' row is recorded/deferred, not dropped.

merged.title: confirmContribution can be replayed after a refund to restore "paid" and mint a fresh bird pick
merged.reasoning: Confirmed and distinct from C-084 (different writer, different trigger; C-084 covers only the webhook). confirmContribution at src/app/(main)/support/actions.ts:181-185 is check-then-write: if (contribution.status !== "paid") { update({ status: "paid", paidAt: new Date() }) }. Any non-paid state — including terminal 'refunded'/'disputed' — transitions back to 'paid'. The idempotency token is the HMAC triple (order_id, payment_id, signature); verifyPaymentSignature (actions.ts:159) is HMAC(orderId|paymentId) with no timestamp/expiry, so it is valid forever and was handed to the payer's own browser at checkout (visible in their network tab). The ownership check (actions.ts:176) passes because it is their own row. So a member who gives ₹500, spends the pick, then obtains a refund can replay confirmContribution with their saved triple: row returns to 'paid' with paidAt=now, the refunded amount re-enters every status='paid' sum, and paidAt > birdPickedAt re-opens a bird pick (actions.ts:244-249) — a repeatable refund-and-replay loop. Trigger is deliberate attacker action (replaying a server action with saved params after a refund), not a normal path, so Medium not High; the real harm is self-serve re-inflation of public/admin totals (the bird is cosmetic).
merged.repro: Rolled-back txn: BEGIN; UPDATE "Contribution" SET status='refunded' WHERE id=<row>; reason through actions.ts:181 (refunded !== 'paid' is true) → update to paid. Or test-mode: pay, capture the confirmContribution payload from the network tab, refund in the dashboard, replay the action with the same payload in the same session — row reads paid, fresh paidAt, /pick-bird admits again.
merged.fix: Replace the guard at actions.ts:181 with a positive predicate that only admits the source states: transition to 'paid' only when contribution.status is 'created' or 'failed' (mirror of the C-084 webhook fix). Refunded/disputed must be a no-op.
merged.gate: Unit test on confirmContribution's transition predicate (or the shared state-machine test from C-084) asserting a refunded/disputed row stays put when confirm is replayed.

merged.title: Dispute-won and dispute-closed events are ignored, so a chargeback the owner WINS stays un-counted forever
merged.reasoning: Confirmed by grep: 'disputed' is written only at src/app/api/razorpay/webhook/route.ts:229-233 and read only as a display label/filter in admin/support/page.tsx:37,117,119 and the audit label. NO writer anywhere moves a row out of 'disputed' (or 'refunded') — the full set of Contribution.status writers is create→created, confirm/captured→paid, failed→failed, refund/dispute→refunded/disputed, plus an admin merge that only reassigns userId and retention that deletes; none resolve a dispute. The acted allowlist (route.ts:126-141) is payment.captured / payment.failed / refund.processed / payment.dispute.created only, so payment.dispute.won and payment.dispute.closed fall into the acknowledged-and-dropped 200 branch (route.ts:142-144). dispute.created un-counts (paid→disputed) but a won/closed dispute — money the owner kept — leaves the row stranded at 'disputed' forever, permanently under-counting 'Given, all time' and the recovery bar with no in-app remedy (hand SQL only). Real state-machine dead-end. Downgraded Medium→Low: disputes on an alumni donation page are rare, it needs a dispute raised AND resolved in the merchant's favour, and the error direction is conservative (under-count, never over-count).
merged.repro: grep for 'disputed' across src shows one writer (route.ts:229) and no reader that transitions out of it; the acted allowlist (route.ts:126-141) omits payment.dispute.won/closed, so those events hit the 200-and-drop path at route.ts:143. A row set to 'disputed' has no code path back to 'paid'.
merged.fix: Add payment.dispute.won and payment.dispute.closed to a handler that transitions status back to 'paid' only from 'disputed' (updateMany where status:'disputed'), writing an audit line; treat payment.dispute.lost as leaving it un-counted (already correct). Consider an admin control to correct a stuck status so the fallback is not raw SQL.
merged.gate: Extend the webhook state-machine test to assert a dispute.won/closed event on a 'disputed' row restores 'paid'.

merged.title: A partial refund un-counts the entire contribution: refund.processed never reads the refund amount
merged.reasoning: Confirmed. The refund branch (route.ts:222-245) flips the WHOLE row to status:'refunded' on any refund.processed, and the audit detail says '${contribution.amount} paise no longer counted as given' (route.ts:243) — the FULL contribution amount. Nothing reads the refund amount: the WebhookPayment type (route.ts:64-70) models only the payment entity, not event.payload.refund.entity.amount, and event is typed at route.ts:114 with no refund payload at all. Since every sum filters status='paid' (support/page.tsx:41 etc.), a partial refund (e.g. ₹100 back on a ₹5,000 gift, one text field in the Razorpay dashboard) erases the entire ₹5,000 from the public recovery bar, 'Given, all time', the month tile, and the member's perk ledger — the paid sum in chooseBird (actions.ts:224-233) can drop below PERK_MIN_PAISE over a token partial refund. Reachable by an ordinary owner dashboard action. Medium: an edge action (partial refunds are unusual on a donation page) whose effect is a wrong (under-counted) total plus a real member-visible perk-eligibility loss; direction conservative but the accounting is simply wrong.
merged.repro: Code trace: route.ts:229-233 transitions status:'refunded' unconditionally and route.ts:243 audits contribution.amount (the full gift); event JSON.parse at route.ts:116 into the type at route.ts:114 never surfaces payload.refund.entity.amount. Live: test mode, pay ₹500, refund ₹100 from the dashboard — refund.processed flips the row to 'refunded' and /support's bar drops by 500, not 100.
merged.fix: Parse event.payload.refund.entity.amount. For a partial refund, do not move the row to 'refunded'; instead subtract the refunded paise (a refundedAmount column, or a separate ledger row) so sums count amount minus refunded. Reserve the full 'refunded' transition for refund.amount === contribution.amount. Audit the actual refunded amount, not contribution.amount.
merged.gate: Unit test feeding a refund.processed payload with refund.amount < contribution.amount and asserting the counted total drops by exactly the refunded paise, not the whole gift.

merged.title: First-audit Low 116 is only half-fixed: the browser confirm path still leaves failureReason (and never sets method) on a retried-then-successful payment
merged.reasoning: Confirmed. The audit-Low-116 hygiene fix (clear failureReason, carry method on the transition to paid) landed only in the webhook captured branch (route.ts:167-174 sets method and failureReason:null). confirmContribution's update (actions.ts:182-185) writes only { status, razorpayPaymentId, paidAt } — it never clears failureReason and never sets method. Reachable sequence, all in-code: first attempt fails → payment.failed webhook writes status='failed' + failureReason (route.ts:210-219); payer retries inside the same modal and succeeds; the browser callback (confirmContribution) usually wins the race and moves failed→paid via actions.ts:181-185, leaving failureReason intact and method untouched; the later payment.captured then matches nothing (route.ts:164 status:{ not:'paid' } now false). Admin consequence verified: the Ledger renders r.failureReason in red text-destructive for ANY row including paid ones (admin/support/page.tsx:303-307), so the 'Given' section shows a paid gift with a stale red error line, and the 'Most used' tile counts r.method ?? 'unknown' (page.tsx:132,168-171) so the gift lands as 'unknown'. Low: admin/owner-facing only, not member-facing, and needs the failed webhook processed before the successful retry's confirm; but a genuine, reachable field-hygiene defect where the two converging writers disagree.
merged.repro: Compare actions.ts:182-185 (data: { status, razorpayPaymentId, paidAt } — no failureReason clear, no method) against route.ts:167-174 (method set, failureReason: null). A row written 'failed' with a failureReason by route.ts:210-219, then moved to 'paid' by confirmContribution, retains failureReason and the failed method; admin/support/page.tsx:303-307 prints that red line under a paid gift. Read-only: the 220ebec diff shows the clearing landed only in route.ts.
merged.fix: In confirmContribution's update (actions.ts:184) add failureReason: null and set method from the successful payment (pass method through from the Razorpay success handler, or accept webhook backfill); at minimum clear failureReason so a paid row never shows a red reason.
merged.gate: Test asserting that after a failed→paid transition via confirmContribution the row has failureReason=null; a shape assertion that both paid-writers set the same field set.

merged.title: A refund does not revoke the bird already picked with that money
merged.reasoning: Not a confirmed defect. Verified the mechanism: the refund/dispute branch (route.ts:222-245) writes only { status } and never touches User.birdOverride / birdPickedAt, and chooseBird (actions.ts:210-267) is the sole writer of birdOverride, so a refunded supporter keeps their picked bird. But the finder itself declines to call this a defect ('flagged as a possible deliberate-by-omission policy rather than a certain defect... the fix session should get an owner ruling'). The only consequence is that a fully-refunded member keeps a COSMETIC bird they themselves chose; no data loss, no wrong money total, no stability impact, and future re-picks are correctly blocked because the paid sum drops below the floor (actions.ts:233). Per the audit's false-positive exclusions this is speculative with no concrete member-harm or stability consequence, and a missing comment is not itself a bug. This is an owner product-policy question (revoke the perk on refund, yes/no), not a code defect — it belongs in FEATURES / an owner decision, not the bug list.

merged.title: confirmContribution (and the webhook's captured branch) can flip a refunded/disputed contribution back to paid, re-inflating the recovery total and regranting a bird pick
merged.reasoning: Same root cause as C-084 and C-085, reported as the union of both. C-123 describes the incomplete terminal-state predicate in BOTH writers: confirmContribution's if (contribution.status !== 'paid') (actions.ts:181, = C-085) and the webhook captured branch's status:{ not:'paid' } (route.ts:163-164, = C-084), both allowing refunded/disputed → paid with a fresh paidAt and a regranted bird pick. The webhook half duplicates C-084 (earliest id); the confirmContribution half duplicates C-085. Marked duplicateOf C-084 as the earliest canonical; both canonicals are CONFIRMED and carry the fix.

merged.title: Razorpay refund/dispute arriving before the capture event is acknowledged with 200 and permanently lost
merged.reasoning: Same root cause as the 'mirror half' C-084 already names and validates: a refund.processed / dispute.created arriving while the row is still 'created' (capture delayed/retrying, browser callback lost) matches nothing at route.ts:230-233 (guard status:'paid'), moved.count=0, falls through to 200 at route.ts:248, so Razorpay never resends and a later payment.captured lands the row on 'paid' with the reversal permanently unrecorded and no audit line (writeAudit at route.ts:238 is inside moved.count===1). C-151 adds the useful nuance that the dropped reversal is also un-audited, which the canonical fix should honour. Marked DUPLICATE of C-084 (earliest, which explicitly covers this mirror), but note for the fix session: this half needs its OWN change (defer/persist or non-2xx the reversal on a not-yet-paid row) distinct from the resurrection predicate-narrowing — do not conflate the two fixes.

merged.title: Staged direct-upload objects are never reclaimed: no sweeper, no lifecycle rule, and several refusal paths skip cleanup
merged.reasoning: Verified. contributePhotoDirect returns on rate-limit refusal at collection/actions.ts:290-291 and on parse failure at :316 with NO delImageByKey, while the quota (:304) and processing-error (:411) paths DO clean up — the asymmetry is exactly as claimed. presign consumes an 'uploads' token (rate-limit.ts:69, 40/h) and so do finalize/contribute, so at the window boundary a presign+PUT succeeds and the very next completion call is 429'd, stranding the staged original; this is a systematically reachable path, not just a crafted one. Confirmed by grep that NO ListObjects/LifecycleConfiguration exists anywhere in src/ or scripts/, and retention.ts's sweep (line 272) only calls drainPendingImagePurges() — it has no bucket-listing step. account-purge's collectImageUrls reads only row-referenced URLs, so staged keys are never enumerable. A browser closed after the PUT (normal abandonment) or a dropped connection before finalize both leak the staged original permanently.
merged.repro: collection/actions.ts:290-291 (rate-limit return, no cleanup) and :316 (parse return, no cleanup) vs :304 and :411 (which do clean up). retention.ts:272 is the only drain and reads PendingImagePurge only. No ListObjects in tree.
merged.fix: Delete the staged key on every refusal path in contributePhotoDirect/finalize (rate-limit and parse branches), and/or add an R2 lifecycle rule expiring staging/ and collection/*-o.* objects after N days as a backstop. Consider a nightly reconciliation that lists the staging prefix and deletes objects with no finalize.
merged.gate: A unit test asserting delImageByKey is called before every non-success return in contributePhotoDirect; owner confirmation of an R2 lifecycle rule on staging/ and *-o.* prefixes.

merged.title: Processed uploads orphan whenever the referencing row is never written; no DB-to-R2 reconciliation exists
merged.reasoning: Verified multiple orphan paths. (1) /api/upload/route.ts loop pushes url after putImage (:149); a later file failing isImageFile/HEIC/size (:84-105, before the try) or sniff/sharp (in the try) returns 400/422 while earlier files' objects stay stored with no cleanup. (2) finalize/route.ts:116 has the same shape — an earlier file's processed webp is orphaned when a later file 422s (the finally only deletes STAGED keys, not the processed output). (3) prisma.photo.create sits OUTSIDE the try in both contributePhoto (:218) and contributePhotoDirect (:418); a DB throw there leaves url+thumbUrl already stored and orphaned, and the try's catch (which deletes the staged key) never runs for a create failure. A partial Promise.all putImage (one of the two succeeds, other throws) also strands the successful object. (5) editPost (feed/actions.ts:~525) writes imagesUpdate={images: allowed} which can DROP a draft image with no delImage/PendingImagePurge for the removed URL — confirmed there is no removed-URL collection in that block. No reverse index exists (no ListObjects) so once a URL leaves every row the bytes are unreachable; account-purge's collectImageUrls reads current rows only.
merged.repro: route.ts:149 push-after-store with early error returns; finalize/route.ts:116; photo.create outside try at collection/actions.ts:218 and :418; editPost drops images at feed/actions.ts allowed-filter with no purge-queue write.
merged.fix: Wrap photo.create in the same try (or write a PendingImagePurge row for the just-stored objects on any post-store failure); in the multi-file loops, track successfully-stored URLs and delete/queue them on an early error; in editPost, diff old vs new images and queue removed URLs into PendingImagePurge.
merged.gate: Tests: (a) a two-file /api/upload where file 2 is corrupt asserts file 1's object is deleted or queued; (b) editPost removing an image queues the old URL; (c) photo.create failure queues the two stored objects.

merged.title: Blank-MIME images (explicitly supported per audit Low 41) are hard-refused by the direct upload path instead of falling back
merged.reasoning: Verified. presign/route.ts:75 does `contentType ? EXT_BY_TYPE[contentType] : undefined`; an empty MIME string is falsy → ext undefined → 400 with 'That photo format isn't supported...' (:79-86). directUploadPut (upload-client.ts:45) does `if (status===400 && presign.error) throw new Error(presign.error)` — a hard throw, not a null-fallback, so the caller surfaces the message and stops. Meanwhile isImageFile (upload-shared.ts:40-43) deliberately ACCEPTS a blank type when the filename extension is an image (the audit Low 41 fix, whose comment explicitly says refusing blank-MIME 'left the member holding a photograph the site would not take'). So a valid JPEG that a mobile browser reports with an empty MIME passes the client's own is-an-image check, then is hard-refused at presign with a wrong 'unsupported format' message and never falls back to the byte-sniffing classic route. Since R2 is configured in production, the direct path runs first for every upload, so this is the live behavior, not a fallback edge.
merged.repro: POST {kind:'collection', contentType:'', bytes:12345} to /api/upload/presign → 400 'format isn't supported'. Client: a File{type:''} with an image filename passes isImageFile but directUploadPut throws on the 400.
merged.fix: In presign, when contentType is empty/outside EXT_BY_TYPE but the request is otherwise valid, answer {direct:false} so the client falls back to the classic route that sniffs real bytes; or have directUploadPut return null (fall back) rather than throw when the 400 is specifically the unsupported-format message for a blank contentType.
merged.gate: A test that a presign call with contentType:'' returns direct:false (or that the client falls back), and an e2e upload of a blank-MIME JPEG succeeds.

merged.title: contributePhotoDirect reads unrotated metadata (its comment lies): EXIF-portrait photos over 40MP are over-shrunk to roughly half the pixel budget
merged.reasoning: The comment lies and the code over-shrinks EXIF-rotated large photos. Confirmed against the installed sharp 0.35.3: metadata() calls sharp.metadata(this.options) (dist/input.cjs) which reads the INPUT header and does NOT execute pending pipeline ops, so `.rotate().metadata()` returns the same width/height as `.metadata()`; the type defs (index.d.ts:1233-1235) state width/height are 'EXIF orientation is not taken into consideration', with the upright values only in `.autoOrient.width/height` (:1238-1242). So at collection/actions.ts:375-376, `upright` holds STORED (unrotated) dims, contradicting the comment at :373-374. For orientation 5-8 the areaFit box is transposed relative to the actual rotated pipeline image. Worked example: 8160x6144 stored, orientation 6 (50.1MP): areaFit={7287,5487} (landscape); the rotated image is 6144x8160 (portrait); `.resize(7287,5487,{fit:'inside'})` scales by min(7287/6144,5487/8160)=0.6725 → ~4132x5487 ≈ 22.7MP, versus the intended ~40MP if autoOrient dims were used. Silent ~43% resolution loss in an archive whose stated purpose is full resolution.
merged.repro: sharp(x).rotate().metadata() returns the unswapped width/height (proven via dist/input.cjs reading this.options + index.d.ts:1233-1235). storedPixelFit(8160,6144) → {7287,5487}; rotated 6144x8160 fit inside that box = ~22.7MP not ~40MP.
merged.fix: Compute areaFit from the upright dimensions: `const upright = await sharpImage(original).rotate().metadata(); storedPixelFit(upright.autoOrient.width, upright.autoOrient.height)` (or just autoOrient.*), and correct the comment.
merged.gate: A local sharp test: generate 8160x6144 with EXIF orientation 6, run the resize block, assert output pixels are within ~5% of 40MP (currently ~22.7MP).

merged.title: keyForUrl refuses this bucket's own URLs whenever full R2 credentials are absent, so deletes run from local dev (shared production DB) silently strand production bytes
merged.reasoning: The code mechanism is real but the claimed consequence is not production-facing and depends on an unverifiable dev fact. storage.ts:266 gates host recognition on `useR2` (`const base = useR2 ? publicBaseFor(url) : null`), so in filesystem mode a full https://images.rishivalley.space/... URL matches neither branch → key=null → delImage returns TRUE (no-op). IN PRODUCTION useR2 is true (all five R2 vars set on Vercel), so keyForUrl resolves correctly and there is no production defect. The harm requires BOTH (a) the local dev .env genuinely lacks R2 creds — which I cannot read (env files are off-limits, and if dev DOES carry R2 creds the whole finding evaporates) — AND (b) a dev session actually running a delete against PRODUCTION content (a real member's photo/post) rather than a throwaway account whose dev-uploaded photos are local /uploads/ paths that keyForUrl handles correctly via the url.startsWith('/') branch. Deleting real production rows from a dev box is outside the sanctioned 'throwaway account' testing flow in TRAPS. So this is at most a dev-hygiene trap against the shared DB, not a shipped bug.
merged.repro: N/A until the runtime fact is checked.
merged.fix: If confirmed worth hardening: recognise legacy/current R2 hosts in keyForUrl regardless of useR2 (publicBaseFor already hardcodes the hosts), so a dev-initiated delete resolves the key; OR guard destructive actions from running in a filesystem-mode dev against non-local URLs. Reasoning per repro must be settled first.
merged.gate: Runtime check: (1) inspect dev .env for R2_* vars — if present, REFUTED; (2) if absent, confirm whether any sanctioned dev flow deletes production (non-/uploads/) image rows. Only if both hold is it a Low.

merged.title: adminRemovePhoto (and avatar replace/remove, admin merge) delete bytes best-effort with no PendingImagePurge fallback — a transient R2 failure recreates the exact M11 hole
merged.reasoning: Verified. adminRemovePhoto (collection/actions.ts:669-673) fires Promise.all([delImage(thumbUrl), delImage(url), delImage(originalUrl)]) and discards all three booleans, then returns success; it writes no PendingImagePurge row. The same ignored-boolean, no-queue pattern is at settings/actions.ts:258 (updateAvatar: row set to new url at :256 THEN `if (prev?.photoUrl && prev.photoUrl!==url) await delImage(prev.photoUrl)`) and :276 (removeAvatar: photoUrl nulled at :274 then delImage), and admin/people/actions.ts:389 (`await delImage(source.photoUrl)`). By contrast declinePhoto/deletePost write PendingImagePurge inside a transaction and let the nightly sweep retry. So on a transient R2 failure at any of these four sites, the 'removed' bytes survive at their permanent public URL with only a console line and nothing to retry — the M11 hole for the failure case. updateAvatar additionally races itself: two concurrent calls both read the same `prev`, both update, both delImage(prev), and the losing new object becomes nobody's prev → orphaned. Severity Low because it needs an R2 failure (uncommon) and the collection row keeps its URLs (recoverable); the GDPR/privacy angle on removeAvatar gives it teeth but not more than Low.
merged.repro: collection/actions.ts:669-673, settings/actions.ts:258 & :276, admin/people/actions.ts:389 — delImage return value unused, no PendingImagePurge write. Contrast declinePhoto:620-630.
merged.fix: At each site, either check the boolean and write a PendingImagePurge row on false (mirroring declinePhoto), or unconditionally enqueue the URLs and drain — so the nightly sweep retries. For updateAvatar's self-race, serialize or capture prev atomically before update.
merged.gate: Test asserting a failed delImage at adminRemovePhoto/updateAvatar/removeAvatar leaves a PendingImagePurge row; grep guard that these four sites either read the boolean or enqueue.

merged.title: A >40MP panorama with aspect ratio above ~6.7:1 fails WebP encode: the areaFit branch bypasses the 16383px dimension ceiling
merged.reasoning: Verified. contributePhotoDirect resize at collection/actions.ts:378-386 uses `areaFit ? areaFit.width : WEBP_MAX_DIM` — i.e. when the image is >40MP (areaFit non-null) the WEBP_MAX_DIM 16383 side-cap is BYPASSED, not combined. storedPixelFit (image.ts:70-82) preserves aspect ratio by area only, so a high-aspect >40MP input keeps a side above 16383. Worked example: 25000x2000 (50MP, ratio 12.5) → scale sqrt(40/50)=0.894 → areaFit={22360,1788}; `.resize(22360,1788,{fit:'inside'})` on the 25000x2000 input yields ~22360x1788, width 22360 > WebP's hard 16383 limit, so `.webp()` throws. describeProcessingError has no branch matching that libvips message → generic 'Could not process the photo...' and the staged original is deleted (:411). Trigger: w*h>40e6 AND aspect>16383^2/40e6≈6.71 — a legal stitched panorama inside every stated ceiling. Rare, hence Low.
merged.repro: Generate a 25000x2000 image, run the :375-386 block: areaFit={22360,1788}; resize output width 22360 > 16383; .webp() throws.
merged.fix: Clamp areaFit dims to WEBP_MAX_DIM before the resize (fit:'inside' preserves aspect), e.g. resize(min(areaFit.width,16383), min(areaFit.height,16383)); or always pass both the area box and 16383 as an outer min.
merged.gate: Local sharp test asserting a 25000x2000 input stores successfully (no throw) with both sides <=16383.

merged.title: Collection Load-more duplicates tiles (React key collision) when a photo is inserted between page fetches
merged.reasoning: Verified. handleLoadMore (collection-client.tsx:183) does `setPhotos(prev => [...prev, ...data.photos])` with no id-dedupe, and the masonry map keys on `p.id` (:421). loadPhotos uses offset pagination `skip: page*24` (actions.ts:536) and re-runs the full sort per page, so an insert sorting before the current window (any new approval under the default newest-first) shifts rows down one: the last tile of page 1 returns as the first row of page 2, producing a duplicate React key (console error) and a doubled tile that the viewer's index navigation also shows. B-122 fixed only the tie-ordering half (orderBy now ends in id, comment at actions.ts:507-518); the insert-drift half survives. Precondition is the product working (someone contributing/approving while another browses), but blast radius is a cosmetic duplicate tile + key warning, so Low.
merged.repro: Two sessions: load /collection page 1, approve an auto-approved photo from admin, click Load more — the boundary tile re-renders with a duplicate key={p.id}.
merged.fix: Dedupe on append: `setPhotos(prev => { const seen=new Set(prev.map(p=>p.id)); return [...prev, ...data.photos.filter(p=>!seen.has(p.id))]; })`. Cursor pagination would remove the drift entirely but dedupe is the minimal fix.
merged.gate: A test/e2e that appending an overlapping page renders no duplicate id and logs no React key warning.

merged.title: MAX_INPUT_PIXELS comment claims 'a full 108MP shot is under this' — 108,000,000 > 100,000,000, so 108MP phone-mode photos are refused with a misleading generic error
merged.reasoning: Confirmed comment-vs-code arithmetic drift plus a misleading error. image.ts:24 sets MAX_INPUT_PIXELS = 100_000_000, and the comment at :18-19 claims 'even a full 108MP shot is under this' — but 12000x9000 = 108,000,000 > 100,000,000, so a full-resolution 108MP photo (Samsung/Xiaomi 108MP mode) exceeds the limit and sharp throws 'Input image exceeds pixel limit' during the decode/resize. describeProcessingError (upload-shared.ts:171-194) matches that string against none of its branches (/unsupported image format/, /premature end|truncated|invalid/, isStorageFailure) → generic 'Could not process the photo. Please try a different one, or a JPG or PNG export of it.' — misleading, since a JPG export at the same resolution fails identically. Reachable when the (heavily-compressed) 108MP JPEG is <=20MB. Per rule 2 the comment claim disagreeing with the code beside it is itself a real finding; the misleading copy makes it member-facing (Low, edge case).
merged.repro: 12000x9000 = 108,000,000 > MAX_INPUT_PIXELS (100,000,000). sharp(input,{limitInputPixels:100e6}) throws on decode; describeProcessingError returns the generic branch.
merged.fix: Either raise MAX_INPUT_PIXELS to ~110-120MP (still far under sharp's 268MP default, bomb argument intact) OR fix the comment to stop claiming 108MP fits and add a describeProcessingError branch for /exceeds pixel limit/ that tells the member the photo is too large in pixels (not 'try a different one').
merged.gate: Unit test: describeProcessingError('Input image exceeds pixel limit') returns a size-specific message; and either a raised constant or a corrected comment asserted.

merged.title: Animated GIFs contributed to the Collection are flattened to a still with nothing said — the M15 fix was applied only to /api/upload
merged.reasoning: Verified. The M15 fix (count frames, add a notice) lives ONLY in /api/upload/route.ts:128-133 (the sole importer/caller of countImageFrames — confirmed image.ts exports it and only route.ts calls it). contributePhoto (collection/actions.ts:189) and contributePhotoDirect (:378) both re-encode GIFs via sharpImage without animated:true and never call countImageFrames, so an animated GIF contributed to the Collection is flattened to frame one with no notice (the success toast says only 'Added to the Collection'). finalize/route.ts (the DIRECT post path, primary in production) likewise never counts frames, so every direct-path GIF post is silently flattened too — the M15 notice fires only on the classic proxied route. GIFs are uncommon and the flattening itself was a decided behavior, so this is a missing-sentence regression, Low.
merged.repro: grep: countImageFrames imported/called only in /api/upload/route.ts. Contribute a 2-frame GIF via the dialog → stored .webp is a still, no notice returned.
merged.fix: Call countImageFrames in contributePhoto, contributePhotoDirect and finalize/route.ts and surface the same 'saved as a still picture' notice (contribute actions would return it in the success payload for a toast).
merged.gate: Tests that each of the three paths returns a notice when frames>1.

merged.title: approvePhoto throws raw P2025 when the photo was concurrently declined — the admin is told to check their connection
merged.reasoning: Verified. approvePhoto (collection/actions.ts:591) is a bare `prisma.photo.update({where:{id:photoId}})` with no try/catch. If another admin declined the photo first (declinePhoto deletes the row at :626), the update throws P2025, unhandled, and reaches callAction which shows the generic 'That did not go through. Check your connection and try again.' — a wrong diagnosis inviting a retry on a photo that no longer exists. Neighbouring paths handle their known Prisma errors: declinePhoto pre-reads and answers 'Photo not found' (:608); togglePhotoLove maps P2003/P2002 (:581-583); and isRecordNotFound (P2025) exists in prisma-errors.ts:27 but is unused here. Requires two admins moderating the same photo concurrently, so Low.
merged.repro: collection/actions.ts:591 bare update, no catch; isRecordNotFound helper exists (prisma-errors.ts:27) but is not applied. Two admins: decline in one, approve in the other → P2025 → generic toast.
merged.fix: Wrap in try/catch and return 'That photo is no longer here.' on isRecordNotFound(err), matching declinePhoto/togglePhotoLove; or use updateMany and check count===0.
merged.gate: Test that approvePhoto on a missing photoId returns a mapped 'no longer here' error rather than throwing.

merged.title: Collection contributions have no duplicate guard: concurrent double-submission mints two Photo rows (and two stored objects), and the per-account quota is check-then-insert
merged.reasoning: Verified. contributePhotoDirect (create at collection/actions.ts:418) and contributePhoto (:218) have no idempotency key and no unique constraint tying a contribution to its staged object. Two overlapping invocations with the same staged key can both HEAD/getImageBuffer the original before either delImageByKey(input.key) runs (:409), both re-encode, and both create Photo rows with independent createId() object names — a duplicate row in the approval queue and duplicate billed bytes (the sequential case fails safe because the first call deletes the staged original, so the second's getImageBuffer throws). photoQuotaError (:114-120) is count-then-refuse with no DB constraint behind MAX_PHOTOS_PER_ACCOUNT, so N concurrent contributions overshoot the quota by N-1. Blast radius is per-account and admin-moderated, hence Low. Not a duplicate of C-130 (that is about P2025 on stale rows; this is duplicate-creation + quota TOCTOU).
merged.repro: Two contributePhotoDirect calls in one Promise.all with the same staged key → two Photo rows sharing uploaderId; quota set to cap-1 then two concurrent contributions → count exceeds MAX by one.
merged.fix: Make the staged key single-use: record it (e.g. a unique column or a claimed-keys set) and reject a second contribute for the same key; enforce the quota with a conditional insert / a checked count inside a transaction, accepting READ COMMITTED cannot fully close it without a constraint (document the residual as bounded).
merged.gate: Test firing two concurrent contributes on one staged key yields exactly one row; quota test that concurrent contributes cannot exceed MAX by more than the known bound.

merged.title: A family of admin/maintenance writes uses unconditional update/delete on possibly-stale rows and throws raw P2025 instead of answering — two admins moderating together get an unhandled error
merged.reasoning: Grouped finding, verified for its in-batch sites. approvePhoto (collection/actions.ts:591) throwing raw P2025 is the SAME defect as C-074 (overlap — see that id). Beyond it, two more in-batch sites hold: (a) declinePhoto's `tx.photo.delete({where:{id}})` at :626 runs inside a transaction after a findUnique pre-read (:604), so a second concurrent decline that deleted the row between the read and the commit throws P2025 and rolls back the whole action → generic failure toast though the delete already happened; (b) drainPendingImagePurges' failure-path `prisma.pendingImagePurge.update` at account-purge.ts:338 has NO .catch, unlike its success-path delete at :331 which does — if a concurrent drain (a live decline's drain racing the nightly sweep) already removed that row, the update throws P2025 unhandled and aborts the remaining drain loop. prisma-errors.ts:27 provides isRecordNotFound but none of these use it. All are admin/maintenance-facing (confusing error surface, not corruption), so Low. The other listed sites (adminHidePost, blockWrite, adminUpdatePerson, dismissMail) are outside this batch and belong to other validators.
merged.repro: collection/actions.ts:591 & :626 bare/uncaught delete-or-update; account-purge.ts:338 update with no .catch vs :331 with .catch. isRecordNotFound (prisma-errors.ts:27) unused.
merged.fix: Convert to updateMany/deleteMany or catch isRecordNotFound at approvePhoto and declinePhoto's tx delete; add a .catch (like the success path) to drainPendingImagePurges' failure-path update at :338 so a row taken by a concurrent drain does not abort the loop.
merged.gate: Tests: concurrent decline/decline and approve/decline return a mapped sentence not a throw; a drain whose failure-path row was concurrently deleted completes without aborting.

merged.title: delImage's failure boolean is ignored on the moderation and avatar paths - 'removed' bytes can silently survive with no worklist
merged.reasoning: Same root cause and same four call sites as C-069: delImage's boolean discarded with no PendingImagePurge fallback at adminRemovePhoto (collection/actions.ts:669-673), updateAvatar (settings/actions.ts:258), removeAvatar (:276) and adminMergeUsers (admin/people/actions.ts:389). C-069 is the earlier id and is fully validated there (CONFIRMED, Low). This is the same defect reported from the silent-failure angle.

merged.title: Photo viewer download fetch never checks res.ok - an error response is saved as the photo
merged.reasoning: Verified. image-viewer.tsx download() (:184-191) does `const res = await fetch(current.src); const blob = await res.blob();` with no res.ok check; the catch at :192 only fires on network/CORS rejection, so a 404 (deleted object) or 5xx resolves and the error body (R2/CDN XML or HTML) is saved to a file named like the photo (name.webp). The member 'successfully' downloads a broken file and only discovers it will not open later. Reachable when the underlying object was deleted (adminRemovePhoto removes bytes while a stale/cached page or a coverPhoto reference still points at the URL). Cosmetic-with-teeth, Low.
merged.repro: image-viewer.tsx:184-191 missing res.ok; open the viewer on a URL whose object was deleted, press Download → saved file is the error document.
merged.fix: After fetch, `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(String(res.status))` so control falls into the catch (open in new tab / show error) instead of saving the error body.
merged.gate: A test that download() on a 404 response takes the fallback path rather than creating a blob download.

merged.title: Direct-upload presign fallback is still fully silent - the failure mode that hid for weeks has no witness even now
merged.reasoning: Verified as an observability gap with a documented, non-speculative precedent. directUploadPut's two catches (upload-client.ts:38-40 on presign, :55-60 on a blocked PUT) both return null with zero logging; the caller then silently downscales in-browser and proxies through the server's ~4.5MB cap. TRAPS.md records that this exact silent fallback concealed that 'direct uploads had never actually worked in production' until 2026-08-21, and storage.ts:150 itself warns a new origin will 'quietly take the slower proxied path instead of failing loudly.' The concrete stability/quality consequence I can name: a future CSP/CORS/preview-origin regression makes every browser upload store a browser-downscaled copy instead of the full original (the sole purpose of presigning), with no witness — precisely the weeks-long concealment the incident write-up describes. It is not a current correctness bug, so Low, but it is a cheap, warranted fix given the recorded history.
merged.repro: upload-client.ts:38-40 and :55-60 return null with no console output; TRAPS.md's 2026-08-21 account of the silent fallback.
merged.fix: Add a console.warn in both catches naming the failure (presign network error / blocked PUT origin), so a recurrence is diagnosable from the browser console; optionally a lightweight client beacon counting fallbacks.
merged.gate: A test/assertion that a blocked PUT emits a warning; manual: remove the S3 endpoint from connect-src in a dev build and confirm the fallback now logs.

merged.title: copyPostImagesToCollection can reject despite its 'resolves rather than throwing' contract, and a partial failure orphans fresh R2 objects
merged.reasoning: Verified both halves. copyPostImagesToCollection's doc (collection-intake.ts:36-41) promises 'the whole thing resolves rather than throwing' because it runs in after() with nobody to tell — but the two top-level reads run OUTSIDE any try/catch: user.findUnique (:57) and photo.count (:69). If either throws, the after() callback rejects (only Next's generic after-error log records it) and the member's ticked 'Also add to the Collection' silently does nothing — the comment overstates the guarantee (comment-vs-code drift). Separately, inside the per-image map both putImage calls (:101-108) can succeed and then prisma.photo.create (:111) throw, landing in the catch at :133 — two freshly-PUT R2 objects with no row and no PendingImagePurge entry, orphaned permanently (same class as C-064 but a distinct site + the lying comment). Runs post-response, best-effort, so Low.
merged.repro: collection-intake.ts:57 & :69 outside try; :101-111 putImage-then-create where a create throw at :111 orphans copiedUrl+thumbUrl with no cleanup at the :133 catch.
merged.fix: Wrap the two pre-loop reads in the same total-resolution try (or return 0 on throw); in the loop catch, delImage/queue the just-stored copiedUrl and thumbUrl before returning false. Correct the comment to scope the guarantee to the mapped section.
merged.gate: Test that a photo.create failure inside the loop leaves no orphan (object deleted or PendingImagePurge row written), and that a pre-loop read failure resolves rather than rejecting.

merged.title: Collection 'Load more' lacks the stale-response generation guard its two siblings have: a filter change mid-flight stitches two result sets together
merged.reasoning: Verified. collection-client.tsx has no generation/stale-response guard on load-more, unlike its siblings post-feed.tsx (listGeneration) and directory-client.tsx. handleLoadMore (:174-192) captures `next=page+1` and appends unconditionally with `setPhotos(prev => [...prev, ...data.photos])` (:183) and adopts the response's hasMore/total/page (:184-186); it has no `cancelled` flag (the filter effect at :148-172 has one only for ITS OWN fetch). So if the user changes When/Part-of-school/search/sort while a Load-more is in flight: the filter effect fires (setLoading(true), setPage(0), fetch page 0 of NEW filters, setPhotos(newData)), then the in-flight OLD-filter response resolves and appends the old query's page onto the new page-0 set — interleaving two different result sets, setting total to the old query's count, and setting page to the OLD next value against the NEW filters so every subsequent Load-more uses the wrong offset (skip/repeat). Offset pagination amplifies it. Also no id-dedupe, so an overlapping page can duplicate key={p.id}. Window is narrow (only during an in-flight Load-more click), and the two guarded siblings prove the pattern is expected, so Medium.
merged.repro: Throttle network, click Load more on /collection, immediately change the When filter → grid shows photos not matching the new filter, total disagrees, and subsequent Load-more skips/repeats. Code: collection-client.tsx:174-192 has no generation ref and no dedupe.
merged.fix: Mirror post-feed's listGeneration: bump a ref in the filter effect, capture it in handleLoadMore, and ignore the response if the ref changed; also dedupe the append by id. fetchPage identity already changes with filters, so the guard can key off that.
merged.gate: An e2e (or unit with a delayed action) asserting a filter change during an in-flight Load-more discards the stale page and leaves total/page consistent with the new filters.

merged.title: Demo: contact editing, admission number, and photo removal fail with a misleading 'check your connection' error
merged.reasoning: Verified the full chain. EDITABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS (src/lib/demo.ts:120-147) does NOT contain showEmail, phone, phones, admissionNumber, or photoUrl, yet schema.prisma:30/36/47/17 confirm all four are real User columns. updateContactMethods (src/components/profile/profile-actions.ts:307-331) writes a data object that UNCONDITIONALLY includes showEmail (boolean), phone (string|null) and phones (string|null) on every call. isOwnProfileEdit (demo.ts:241-244) iterates data keys and returns false on the first non-allowlisted key (showEmail), so demoWriteAllowed('User','update',...) is false for EVERY contact save, including one that only touched instagram. The Prisma demo extension (src/lib/prisma.ts:81-84) throws DemoWriteError; profile-actions.ts wraps nothing in try/catch, so it propagates to useAutoSave.run's catch (src/components/profile/pen.tsx:357-358) which sets the misleading 'That did not save. Check your connection.' The demo persona's id is 'demo-visitor' (auth.ts:375-411 returns DEMO_USER_ID) which matches the where.id === DEMO_USER_ID guard, and its own profile renders the editable letterhead (letterhead-profile.tsx:456 commitContacts -> updateContactMethods). Same defect for updateProfileField('admissionNumber') (profile-actions.ts:105-114 writes data.admissionNumber) surfaced via useAutoSave, and for removeAvatar (settings/actions.ts:264-280 writes photoUrl:null with NO IS_DEMO front door, unlike updateAvatar at :195) surfaced via callAction/ACTION_FAILED. Cross-checked that this is not a documented-deliberate closure: docs/spec/demo.md:167-179 lists 'edit their own profile' under 'They can' and says 'All of it is real'. Confirmed tryRosterAutoVerify short-circuits on IS_DEMO (roster.ts:34) so name/year edits DO save, scoping the failure exactly to contacts/admission/photo as the finder claims. Severity Medium not High: demo-only deployment, invented people, no data loss, and most profile fields still save; the harm is a misleading error on an advertised path of the public showcase.
merged.repro: Policy-level (no live needed): demoWriteAllowed('User','update',{where:{id:'demo-visitor'},data:{displayEmail:'a@b.c',showEmail:true,phone:null,phones:null,instagram:null,linkedin:null,facebook:null,links:null}}) === false, and demoWriteAllowed('User','update',{where:{id:'demo-visitor'},data:{admissionNumber:42}}) === false. Live: on DEMO_MODE=1, open /profile/demo-visitor, Edit, change any contact row and blur -> save banner reads 'That did not save. Check your connection.' while name/bio/city edits save fine; server log shows DemoWriteError.
merged.fix: Add showEmail, phone, phones and admissionNumber to EDITABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS in src/lib/demo.ts (they are ordinary scalar profile columns the visitor is meant to edit). Keep photoUrl/coverPhoto out of the set, but give removeAvatar an IS_DEMO front-door sentence the way updateAvatar (settings/actions.ts:195) has, so photo removal returns a written demo message instead of the generic connection error.
merged.gate: Extend src/lib/demo.test.mjs with assertions that demoWriteAllowed('User','update', <full updateContactMethods payload incl showEmail/phone/phones>) === true and the admissionNumber payload === true, pinning the allowlist against future column drift.

merged.title: Demo visitors cannot save the profile contact block or admission number: EDITABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS drifted behind the schema (showEmail, phone, phones, admissionNumber missing)
merged.reasoning: Identical root cause to C-044: EDITABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS (demo.ts:120-147) drifted behind the schema and refuses updateContactMethods (showEmail/phone/phones) and updateProfileField('admissionNumber'). C-110 adds the same details from the demo-deployment angle plus the settings/actions.ts updateUserProfile 'latent sibling' (which has no live UI caller since the settings page was removed, so it is not independently member-visible). C-044 is the earlier id and canonical. C-110 rated it High; corrected to the canonical Medium (demo-only, no data loss, most fields save).

merged.title: Demo has zero rate limiting plus unbounded allowlisted creates; a disk-fill makes the nightly reset itself fail (30s transaction cannot clear a bloated table), so the demo cannot self-heal
merged.reasoning: The three code facts are confirmed: (1) rateLimit/hasBudget/consume all short-circuit open when IS_DEMO (rate-limit.ts:156,175,190) and the demo project deliberately has no Upstash keys (:113-118) - this is documented as intentional in the header comment; (2) ALLOWED_WRITE_MODELS (demo.ts:63-80) permits unbounded anonymous create on Post/Comment/Like etc., and postSchema allows up to POST_CONTENT_MAX.letter = 20000 chars (validators.ts:214,222); (3) seedDemo's clear phase runs post.deleteMany({}) et al inside ONE transaction with timeout SEED_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000 (seed.ts:74,519-520). But the load-bearing CONSEQUENCE - that an attacker can grow a table large enough that the reset's DELETE exceeds 30s (or the pg adapter's 20s client query_timeout), rolls back, and permanently breaks self-heal - is a runtime/scale claim the finder itself concedes needs a timing test. It is unproven from code whether the attacker-achievable row count times out, and free-tier disk fill may intervene first (Supabase may go read-only, a different failure). The abuse also requires a sustained deliberate high-volume attack against a separate demo DB of invented people with a documented 'scribble on a sandbox that restores itself' threat model. Real but contingent; default to NEEDS-LIVE rather than a hopeful CONFIRMED. Severity corrected from Medium to Low absent proof of easy reach; would rise to Medium if the live check shows the DELETE times out at an achievable scale.

merged.title: demoWriteAllowed passes nested writes into disallowed models wholesale when the top-level model is allowlisted, contradicting the guard's 'born blocked, not born exposed' contract
merged.reasoning: Mechanically the claim is accurate: for a model in ALLOWED_WRITE_MODELS, demoWriteAllowed returns true at demo.ts:206 without inspecting args, so demoWriteAllowed('Post','update',{data:{author:{update:{role:'admin'}}}}) === true and the PhotoLove nested-Photo-create === true. But the finder itself states this is NOT exploitable: no reachable server action passes visitor-controlled data into a nested-write position (actions build their own data literals, images go through ownedUploadUrls, the only nested creates are group.members - blocked at the Group level - and poll options which are allowlisted). Per the audit's false-positive exclusions, a defense-in-depth gap with no reachable member-visible or stability consequence is REFUTED. The comment-vs-code-drift angle also does not hold: the unit test 'a visitor cannot smuggle a write through a nested relation' (demo.test.mjs:196-214) asserts ONLY the User-model case (data:{...posts:{create}}, data:{places:{deleteMany}}), and its inline comment describes exactly that reachable User-branch behaviour (isOwnProfileEdit rejecting object-valued data at demo.ts:243) - the code beside the comment does what the comment says, so there is no lie to confirm. The test name is broader than its body, but that is not a bug that hides a reachable defect. Kept at the finder's Low.

merged.title: Rate limiters fail open with console-only evidence - a Redis outage silently disables every limit in the app
merged.reasoning: Verified both halves. (1) rateLimit (rate-limit.ts:162-165), hasBudget (:181-184) and consume (:195-197) each catch every error, console.error, and return ok/true - fail-open, which the header comment documents as a deliberate availability choice. (2) The observability gap is real: src/instrumentation.ts (the only Sentry setup) calls Sentry.init with no captureConsole/consoleLoggingIntegration and exports onRequestError=captureRequestError, so Sentry only records thrown/unhandled errors and RSC request errors - a caught+logged limiter failure never becomes a Sentry event. Grepped: no captureConsole/consoleLoggingIntegration anywhere. So a sustained Upstash outage or bad creds after an env-var edit silently disables EVERY limiter at once (login-ip, login-account, reauth password-guess door, signup, reset, uploads, reports, contributions, search) with evidence only in per-call Vercel console lines - no Sentry, no admin surface. The finder correctly targets the alerting gap, not the fail-open policy; the header comment settles the fail-open decision but does NOT address sustained-failure alerting, so this is not a documented-deliberate closure. Genuinely a Low hardening/observability finding, not a false alarm: the security consequence (all brute-force protection off, silently) is nameable and the trigger (Upstash misconfig) is a plausible operational event.
merged.repro: Code trace is complete: set an invalid UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL (or drop the creds), exercise login failures past the 30/15m login-ip budget - every attempt passes because limiter.limit() throws, is caught at rate-limit.ts:163, logged, and returns {ok:true}. With SENTRY_DEV=1 no Sentry event is produced (instrumentation.ts has no console-capture integration); the only trace is '[rate-limit] login-ip check failed open' in the Vercel log stream.
merged.fix: On a limiter backend error, emit a throttled Sentry.captureMessage/captureException (e.g. once per N minutes or on a run of consecutive failures) from the catch blocks in rate-limit.ts so a sustained Upstash outage/misconfig surfaces where a human looks, while keeping the fail-open request behaviour unchanged.
merged.gate: Add a small test asserting the limiter catch path invokes a reporter hook on error (inject the reporter), or a manual runbook check that a forced Upstash-creds failure raises a Sentry event.

merged.title: chooseBird's header comment describes the abolished re-pick model the code below refuses
merged.reasoning: Comment-vs-code drift is real. The chooseBird docstring at src/app/(main)/support/actions.ts:206-208 states 'Re-picking is allowed indefinitely. The perk is standing... nothing to meter and no state to corrupt by clicking twice.' The inner gate at actions.ts:236-256 implements the OPPOSITE: one pick per contribution, spent by birdPickedAt (243) and regranted only by a paid contribution with paidAt > birdPickedAt (244-249), else refused (254). The inner block carries the authoritative owner date (2026-08-18) and matches the actual runtime behaviour, so the header docstring is the stale one — exactly the 'a comment can LIE' case the brief says to confirm. Note: the finding's secondary 'double-click / change-your-mind toast' claim is NOT a bug — refusing a second pick without a newer contribution is the intended one-pick-per-contribution design, not a defect. The only real defect here is the stale header comment that a future session would trust to 'fix the gate away'.
merged.repro: Read actions.ts:206-208 (header: re-picking allowed indefinitely) against actions.ts:243-256 (owner 2026-08-18: one pick per contribution, refuses a re-pick without a newer paid contribution). Direct contradiction; the dated inner comment is authoritative.
merged.fix: Rewrite the docstring lines 206-208 to describe the one-pick-per-contribution model (a pick is spent by birdPickedAt and regranted only by a paid contribution newer than the last spend), matching the inner comment. Do not touch the gate.
merged.gate: Code review / a doc-consistency pass; no automatable test (pure comment).

merged.title: Duplicate/out-of-order payment.captured resurrects a refunded contribution to "paid" (and re-grants a bird pick)
merged.reasoning: The captured-branch predicate is genuinely over-broad. route.ts:163-164 runs updateMany({ where: { id, status: { not: "paid" } }, data: { status: "paid", paidAt: new Date(), ... } }). 'refunded' and 'disputed' both satisfy status != 'paid', so a re-delivered payment.captured transitions a reversed row back to 'paid' with a fresh paidAt. This is reachable via the Razorpay dashboard's manual 'resend', or via an auto-retry after a prior non-2xx capture (a DB blip or the unconfigured-secret 500 window) that lands after a refund. Consequences confirmed in code: every money sum filters status='paid' so refunded money re-counts on /support and 'Given, all time'; the fresh paidAt satisfies chooseBird's regrant filter paidAt: { gt: me.birdPickedAt } at actions.ts:249, minting a new pick; and moved.count===1 fires the 'Your contribution came through' notification (route.ts:191-204) after a refund. Downgraded High->Medium: it needs a refund/chargeback (rare, owner-driven) plus a capture redelivery, not a normal-path member action, but it does corrupt the public money total. IMPORTANT: this is RC1 (over-broad captured predicate). The finding's 'mirror half' paragraph (early-refund-lost) is a DIFFERENT defect tracked as C-151 and is NOT fixed by narrowing this predicate.
merged.repro: Rolled-back txn via run-sql.mjs: BEGIN; UPDATE "Contribution" SET status='refunded' WHERE id=<row>; then replicate the captured branch: UPDATE "Contribution" SET status='paid', "paidAt"=now() WHERE id=<row> AND status <> 'paid'; SELECT status,"paidAt" -> row reads 'paid' with a fresh paidAt; ROLLBACK. Live: Razorpay test mode, pay, refund, then dashboard 'resend' the payment.captured event and watch /support and the row.
merged.fix: Narrow the captured WHERE at route.ts:164 to status: { in: ["created", "failed"] } so 'refunded'/'disputed' are terminal for the captured transition. (Apply the sibling fix in confirmContribution — C-085. Does NOT resolve C-151.)
merged.gate: Unit/integration test: a payment.captured event against a 'refunded' or 'disputed' row is a no-op (row stays reversed, no notification, no new pick).

merged.title: confirmContribution can be replayed after a refund to restore "paid" and mint a fresh bird pick
merged.reasoning: Confirmed. verifyPaymentSignature (src/lib/razorpay.ts:131-134) is HMAC-SHA256 over `${orderId}|${paymentId}` with no timestamp/nonce, so the triple handed to the payer's browser at checkout is valid forever. confirmContribution guards only `if (contribution.status !== "paid")` (actions.ts:181) before setting status='paid', paidAt=now (182-185), so 'refunded' and 'disputed' rows transition back to 'paid'. The ownership check (176) passes for the member's own row. A member who paid >=₹500, picked a bird, then obtained a refund or filed a chargeback (webhook moves paid->refunded/disputed) can replay the saved triple: row returns to 'paid', refunded money re-counts in every public/admin total, and fresh paidAt > birdPickedAt reopens the pick (chooseBird actions.ts:249). Repeatable. Attacker-triggerable (not dependent on Razorpay redelivery), but requires dev-tools replay and yields only a decorative bird plus total inflation, so Medium is the right ceiling.
merged.repro: Test mode: pay, capture the confirmContribution payload (order_id/payment_id/signature) from the network tab, refund in the dashboard until the row reads 'refunded', then re-invoke the server action with the same payload in the same session -> row: status='paid', fresh paidAt; /pick-bird re-admits. Read-only: razorpay.ts:131-134 (no timestamp in the HMAC) + actions.ts:181 (guards only against the target state) settle it.
merged.fix: Replace the guard at actions.ts:181 with an explicit source-state check, e.g. only transition when contribution.status is 'created' or 'failed'; treat 'refunded'/'disputed' as terminal no-ops. Mirror of the webhook fix in C-084.
merged.gate: Unit test: confirmContribution against a 'refunded'/'disputed' row leaves it unchanged and returns ok/no-op without minting a pick.

merged.title: Dispute-won and dispute-closed events are ignored, so a chargeback the owner WINS stays un-counted forever
merged.reasoning: Confirmed dead-end. The `acted` allowlist (route.ts:126-141) covers only payment.captured, payment.failed, refund.processed, payment.dispute.created. payment.dispute.won / dispute.closed / dispute.lost fall into the acknowledged-and-dropped branch (route.ts:142-144, return 200). Grep across src/ confirms the ONLY writer of 'disputed' is the webhook else-branch (route.ts:229-233); the admin support surface has no mutation (only page.tsx + loading.tsx — verified the directory), and nothing anywhere moves a row OUT of 'disputed'. So a chargeback the owner WINS (money stayed) leaves the gift permanently un-counted in the recovery bar, 'Given, all time', and the member's history, correctable only by hand-SQL against the shared production DB. Medium: needs a dispute raised AND resolved-in-favour, which is rare for donations, and it under-counts (a legit gift disappears) rather than lying upward, but the only remedy is manual SQL.
merged.repro: route.ts:126-141 lists four events; dispute.won/closed are absent -> route.ts:142-144 returns { received: true } with no write. grep -rn 'disputed' src/ shows writers only in webhook/route.ts and labels/filters in admin/support/page.tsx; no code path sets a 'disputed' row to any other status. Live: send a signed payment.dispute.won to a dev server and observe 200 + unchanged row.
merged.fix: Add payment.dispute.won (and closed-as-won) to `acted` and move 'disputed'->'paid' conditionally (where status: 'disputed'), writing a reversal-restored audit line; keep dispute.lost as reversed. Consider a small admin action to correct a stuck status.
merged.gate: Unit test: a signed payment.dispute.won for a 'disputed' row restores it to 'paid' and re-counts it.

merged.title: A partial refund un-counts the entire contribution: refund.processed never reads the refund amount
merged.reasoning: Confirmed. The refund branch (route.ts:229-233) sets status='refunded' on ANY refund.processed and never inspects the refund amount — the WebhookPayment type (route.ts:64-70) and the parsed event shape (route.ts:114) model only payload.payment.entity, never payload.refund.entity. Because every sum filters status='paid', moving the row to 'refunded' subtracts the FULL contribution.amount regardless of how much was actually refunded. Razorpay supports partial refunds from the dashboard (one text field), and refund.processed fires for them, so a ₹100 refund on a ₹5,000 gift erases the whole ₹5,000 from /support's public bar, 'Given, all time', the month tile, and can drop the member's paid-sum pick eligibility below ₹500. The audit detail even hard-codes the full amount (route.ts:243: `${contribution.amount} paise no longer counted`). Medium: reachable by an ordinary owner dashboard action, but partial refunds on donations are uncommon.
merged.repro: route.ts:229-233 transitions unconditionally; nothing reads event.payload.refund. Test mode: pay ₹500, issue a ₹100 partial refund from the dashboard; refund.processed arrives, row flips to 'refunded', /support's bar and 'Given, all time' drop by ₹500 not ₹100.
merged.fix: Parse event.payload.refund.entity.amount. Only move to 'refunded' when cumulative refunded == full payment amount; for a partial, record the refunded portion (a refundedAmount column, or a 'partially_refunded' state) so sums subtract only what left. Add refund.entity to the parsed event type.
merged.gate: Unit test: a partial refund.processed does not fully un-count the contribution (sum drops by the refunded amount only).

merged.title: First-audit Low 116 is only half-fixed: the browser confirm path still leaves failureReason (and never sets method) on a retried-then-successful payment
merged.reasoning: Confirmed, and broader than the retry framing. confirmContribution's update (actions.ts:182-185) writes only { status, razorpayPaymentId, paidAt } — it never clears failureReason nor sets method, whereas the webhook captured branch does both (route.ts:172, 167). Verified display: /admin/support renders failureReason in red text-destructive (page.tsx:303-306) and shows the status chip ONLY for non-paid rows (page.tsx:288), so a paid row that went failed->paid via the browser callback shows a red error line under a successful gift. Two sub-parts confirmed: (1) failureReason survives only when the payment.failed webhook wrote it before confirmContribution wins (a real but narrower race, since failed only writes from 'created' at route.ts:210-211); (2) method stays NULL on EVERY browser-won payment (the common path, not just retries) — the captured webhook then no-ops because the row is already 'paid' (route.ts:164 predicate) — so the 'Most used' tile (page.tsx:132, 168-171) counts them as 'unknown'. Low: admin-only surface, no member impact; the method-tile degradation is systematic but cosmetic.
merged.repro: Read actions.ts:182-185 (no failureReason clear, no method) vs route.ts:167-173 (both set). Retry case: fail a card attempt (webhook writes 'failed'+failureReason), retry successfully in the same modal on a fast connection so confirmContribution wins the race; /admin/support 'Given' shows the paid row with a red failureReason and no method. Common case: any first-try browser-confirmed payment leaves method NULL -> 'Most used' shows 'unknown'.
merged.fix: In confirmContribution's update add `failureReason: null` and carry `method`. Razorpay's checkout success handler returns razorpay_payment_id/order_id/signature but not method, so pass method through from the client or accept method being set by the webhook only after also making confirmContribution not block it — minimum viable fix is clearing failureReason; ideal fix also records method on the browser path.
merged.gate: Unit test: a failed->paid confirmContribution clears failureReason; assert the paid ledger row carries a method on the browser-confirm path.

merged.title: A refund does not revoke the bird already picked with that money
merged.reasoning: Code behaviour verified; this is a genuine policy gap, not a clear defect (the finder itself flags it as needing an owner ruling). The refund/dispute branch writes only { status } (route.ts:230-233); User.birdOverride and birdPickedAt are untouched, and chooseBird (actions.ts:259-262) is the sole member writer of birdOverride and runs only on a new pick. So a member who paid ₹500, picked a bird, and was fully refunded keeps the paid-only bird indefinitely — while re-picks are correctly blocked once their paid sum drops below PERK_MIN_PAISE. Unlike every other money decision in these files, no comment records this retention as deliberate. Consequence is real but minor (a decorative glyph), so Low, and it warrants an owner decision rather than an assumed fix.
merged.repro: route.ts:230-233 changes status only; grep confirms birdOverride/birdPickedAt are written nowhere in the webhook. A refunded supporter's birdOverride is never cleared, so the bird persists.
merged.fix: Owner ruling required. If revocation is wanted: in the refund/dispute branch, when the member's remaining paid sum drops below PERK_MIN_PAISE, clear birdOverride/birdPickedAt (guard against un-setting a bird still covered by other paid gifts). If retention is intended, add a one-line comment recording the decision so it isn't re-flagged.
merged.gate: N/A until owner decides; then a comment or a test pinning the chosen behaviour.

merged.title: confirmContribution (and the webhook's captured branch) can flip a refunded/disputed contribution back to paid, re-inflating the recovery total and regranting a bird pick
merged.reasoning: Same root causes as already-canonical findings, from a combined angle.
