Real behavior on a public-launch domain: the site ships no crawl policy at all and standard well-known probes bounce into the auth flow. Low ('cosmetic with teeth' for a public release): crawlers are not members and there is no stability consequence, but it is a genuine pre-launch drift with a trivial fix.
merged.repro: curl -i https://rishivalley.space/robots.txt (signed out) -> 307 Location /login rather than a robots policy or a clean 404. Code trace: no robots/sitemap route or public file exists; matcher does not exclude these paths; publicPaths does not list them.
merged.fix: Add app/robots.ts (Next serves it at /robots.txt) and optionally app/sitemap.ts for the six public pages, then exclude /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml from the proxy matcher (or add them to publicPaths). Decide whether /.well-known/* should be allowlisted too.
merged.gate: A test/matcher assertion that /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml are not redirected to /login for a signed-out request.

merged.title: Bare /catchups/join (tokenless) falls through to the [catchupId] route instead of the join page's own dead-link shell
merged.reasoning: Verified the route tree: src/app/catchups/join contains only [token]/page.tsx -- there is NO src/app/catchups/join/page.tsx -- while src/app/(main)/catchups/[catchupId]/page.tsx exists. So the two-segment path /catchups/join resolves to the (main) dynamic segment with catchupId='join', not to any join page. A signed-in member gets the generic loadHome not-found 404; a signed-out visitor matches publicPaths exact '/catchups/join' (proxy.ts:245) and passes the proxy, then hits the (main) layout's bare redirect('/login') (and per C-200, with no next param). Either way the join page's purpose-built 'invite link is not one we recognise' shell (catchups/join/[token]/page.tsx:82-97) -- which exists for a bad/lost token -- is bypassed. Real route-collision edge; Low because the trigger is contrived (the whole token, not just a bad token, must be dropped so the URL shortens to /catchups/join).
merged.repro: Signed in, open /catchups/join -> generic hoopoe 404 (catchupId='join' has no Catch-up). Signed out, open /catchups/join -> bounce to /login. Route tree (find output): catchups/join/[token]/page.tsx exists, catchups/join/page.tsx does not, (main)/catchups/[catchupId]/page.tsx does.
merged.fix: Add src/app/catchups/join/page.tsx that renders the same 'link not recognised' shell (or redirects to /catchups), so the bare tokenless path is owned by the join surface rather than shadowed by the (main) [catchupId] segment.
merged.gate: A route test / e2e asserting GET /catchups/join renders the invite dead-link shell rather than a generic 404 or a login bounce.

merged.title: Launch-day verify-mail backlog: last confirmation sends ~3 days after signup at 300 signups, while the banner promises tomorrow's UTC midnight to everyone
merged.reasoning: The banner-ETA half is a real defect; the backlog-capacity half restates an already-accepted constraint. Verified: effective verify budget is 75/day (email-queue.ts:76 DAILY_CAP=95 minus :87 RESET_RESERVE=20; dailyBudget:406 verifyRemaining = remaining-20). verificationMailState (email-queue.ts:872-874) returns { state:'queued', sendingAt: nextBudgetResetAt() } whenever verifyRemaining<=0, and nextBudgetResetAt (781-785) is pure calendar arithmetic — Date.UTC(y,m,d+1) — with NO queue-depth term. verify-email-banner.tsx:44-58 (sendTimeLabel) renders that ISO as a concrete clock time and line 189 prints 'Your link goes out tomorrow at 5:30 am'. Drain is oldest-first within priority (drainWithLease:734 orderBy priority asc, createdAt asc), so a signup past position ~150 on a >150-signup launch day genuinely waits 2+ UTC days while being shown 'tomorrow'. The ETA is wrong and self-corrects only on the final day before its send. The raw multi-day backlog itself is NOT a new bug: email-queue.ts:31-34 records that the owner designed the queue around Resend's 100/day free plan expecting >100 day-one signups, and 'raise the Resend plan' is a known pre-launch owner action. Downgraded High->Medium: the wrong ETA only manifests past ~150 day-one signups, the mail still arrives (with a fresh token, minted at send per render():564), and the Stage-0 wait is the accepted free-plan consequence.
merged.repro: Code trace: with 300 queued verify rows, rows 76-150 send on UTC day 2, 151-225 on day 3, 226-300 on day 4. On day 1 every one of rows 76-300 loads a page, verificationMailState sees verifyRemaining<=0 and returns sendingAt=nextBudgetResetAt()=day-2 midnight, which the banner prints as 'tomorrow at 5:30 am' — false for everyone past row ~150. nextBudgetResetAt has no term for count(status='queued',kind='verify',createdAt<row.createdAt).
merged.fix: Compute sendingAt from queue position: ceil((count of eligible verify rows ahead of this one) / 75) days forward from the next UTC reset, instead of always nextBudgetResetAt(). Independently, raising the Resend plan before launch removes the backlog. Do not change the banner copy without changing the source value in verificationMailState.
merged.gate: Unit test on a pure sendingAt-from-queue-depth helper: N rows ahead at 75/day must yield ceil(N/75) days, not a constant.

merged.title: Feed load-more dies silently when the cursor post is deleted, hidden, or its author blocked (no M39-style recovery, unlike directory and admin people)
merged.reasoning: The Prisma cursor-at-vanished-row mechanism is proven by the codebase itself. directory/actions.ts:77-105 documents and fixes exactly this (audit M39): 'Prisma's cursor needs the row it names to be INSIDE the filtered set... this query answers nothing for a list with hundreds of rows left', and recovers when rows.length===0 && cursor by re-checking cursor membership and falling back to skip:loaded. The feed keyset branch (feed/actions.ts:1109-1118) does cursor:{id:keysetCursor}, skip:1 with NO such recovery; hasMore (1116) then computes false and nextCursor null, so infinite scroll ends silently though older posts remain. The feed where includes isHidden:false and AUTHOR_IN_GOOD_STANDING (posts.ts:60 = {author:{isBlocked:false}}) plus the deleted-post case, so the exact page-boundary post (the PAGE_SIZE-th, whose id is nextCursor) can leave the set via own-delete, a moderator hide, or the viewer blocking its author. loadComments (feed/actions.ts:1405-1414) carries the identical unrecovered shape for a root whose visibility flips. Medium, not High: it needs the vanished row to be exactly the cursor row, and a feed refresh re-pages from the top and recovers — matching how M39 was treated. The notifications bell (notifications/actions.ts:30-35) shares the shape but is the weakest instance: the KEEP prune is skipped on cursor pages (:44) and the nightly sweep only deletes >365-day rows, so its trigger is remote.
merged.repro: Load feed to exactly PAGE_SIZE posts; from a second account delete (or as admin hide) the last post on the page, or block its author from the viewer account; click Load more. rows=[] because the cursor id no longer matches where; hasMore=false, nextCursor=null; the feed ends although older posts exist. Refresh recovers it.
merged.fix: Mirror directory/actions.ts:91-105 in the feed keyset branch and loadComments: when rows.length===0 && cursor, re-check the cursor still satisfies where; if not, re-query with skip set to the loaded count (offset fallback).
merged.gate: e2e/unit like the existing directory M39 guard: deleting the boundary row must still return the next page, not an empty one.

merged.title: Visit rows are minted from a client-controlled cookie with no throttle: an authed member can create one row per request forever, or write into another member's Visit row
merged.reasoning: Both mechanisms verified. proxy.ts:296-301 takes the visit id from the member's own rv-visit cookie, accepting ANY string matching /^[0-9a-z-]{8,64}$/, and stamps it into x-visit-id. last-seen.ts:115-161 upserts prisma.visit on that id on every authenticated layout render (last-seen.ts:8-9 'Called from the (main) layout... on EVERY authenticated page'); the update branch (141-160) is scoped only to {id:visitId}, never to userId. rate-limit.ts LIMITS (35-100) has NO limiter for page GETs or presence — only login/signup/reset/trivia/posts/comments/uploads/reports/catchups/contributions/reauth/export/search — so nothing throttles Visit creation. (1) An authed member rotating the cookie value per request mints one new Visit row per GET, uncapped: ~660k rows (~500MB at ~750B/row measured in db-sizes-live.json) fills the free-tier disk and takes the DB read-only for everyone. (2) The unscoped update means replaying another member's visit id increments their views and overwrites their endedAt/device/geo. Downgraded High->Medium: it is abuse-only (a normal browser keeps one sliding 30-min cookie = one row), needs a deliberate authenticated attacker in a vouched community, and consequence (2) is impractical — the id is an httpOnly cookie derived from the victim's session token (derivedVisitId), not guessable. The uncapped-write (1) is the real teeth.
merged.repro: Authed throwaway account: send 5 GETs to /feed each with a distinct conforming rv-visit cookie value; SELECT count(*) FROM "Visit" WHERE "userId"=<throwaway> returns 5. No rate limiter is on the path. Sustained at ~20 req/s that is ~1.7M rows/day with the only cleanup being the 180-day sweep.
merged.fix: Derive the visit id server-side from a hash of (userId, 30-min bucket) rather than trusting the cookie, OR scope the upsert to (id AND userId) so a replayed/foreign id cannot update another's row, plus a per-user daily Visit-row cap.
merged.gate: Test: a request whose x-visit-id names a row owned by another userId must not update that row; a per-user row cap must hold under a rotating-cookie loop.

merged.title: Visit table alone approaches the 500MB Supabase free-tier cap at the 2,000-user target (Place already spends 97MB of it)
merged.reasoning: Structural point verified against live numbers. Visit (schema.prisma:1060-1109) is one row per session with ~19 columns (8 free-text) and 3 indexes (PK, @@index([endedAt]), @@index([userId,endedAt])), written by touchLastSeen on every authed render, deleted only when endedAt<now-180d (retention.ts:58 presence=180, :147-151). Unlike ContentView, which schema.prisma:1150-1156 was DELIBERATELY made a bounded counter with the exact reasoning '2,000 members at twenty views a day is 14M rows a year, which is gigabytes on a 500MB plan', Visit was never run through that plan arithmetic. Measured cost is 184kB/243 rows (db-sizes-live.json) = ~757B/row incl. indexes. The project's own stated scale (last-seen.ts:22-23: 2,000 members x 30 views/day) at ~8 views/session is ~7.5k visits/day x 180d ≈ 1.35M rows; even at a conservative 400-500B/row that is ~540-675MB for Visit alone, on top of Place's 97MB, against the 500MB free tier the ContentView comment names. So the fastest-growing telemetry table plausibly blows the plan at target scale. Medium: contingent on reaching a scale the site (52 users) is far from, and resolvable by a plan upgrade or a retention cut, not a correctness defect. Distinct from C-163 (that is abuse-driven; this is legitimate-traffic growth via retention sizing).
merged.repro: Live: SELECT pg_total_relation_size('"Visit"')::float/count(*) FROM "Visit" for the true per-row cost, x steady-state rows (visits/day x 180). If it lands over ~250MB it plus Place's 97MB crosses 500MB.
merged.fix: Halve presence retention from 180 to 90 days (retention.ts:54-57 records the deepest analytics read is 90 days, so no answer shortens), or upgrade the Supabase plan before scaling. Change the window in docs/SECURITY.md retention table first per retention.ts:9-11.
merged.gate: Capacity checklist item; optionally a test that KEEP_DAYS.presence matches the deepest analytics lookback.

merged.title: PostHog free tier (1M events/month) is ~5-8x exceeded at the 2,000-user target; OPERATIONS.md's '600k a year' sizing is two orders of magnitude off at that scale
merged.reasoning: Verified. posthog-provider.tsx has autocapture:true (:74), capture_pageview:'history_change' (:79) and capture_pageleave:true (:80) with no sampling anywhere. The OPERATIONS.md sizing claim is verbatim as reported: OPERATIONS.md:194-195 'Free tier is 1M events a month against usage of maybe 600k a year, so there is no bill to reach' — true at 52 members, but at the mandated 2,000-user scale (project's own model, last-seen.ts:22-23, 20-30 views/day) it is ~40-60k pageviews + as many pageleaves + ~3x autocaptured clicks ≈ 5-9M events/month against the 1M free tier, ~2 orders of magnitude past the doc's figure. Consequence is graceful and NOT member-visible or a stability risk: with no card PostHog stops ingesting at the cap (funnels/paths truncate mid-month); with a card it bills. Low is correct. The crisp, code-verifiable deliverable is the stale OPERATIONS.md sizing line plus the absence of any client-event sampling; contingent on reaching target scale.
merged.repro: posthog-provider.tsx:74-80 shows the three multipliers on with no sample rate. Live confirmation is the PostHog usage dashboard after one active day, extrapolated by member count.
merged.fix: Before scaling: sample autocapture and/or drop capture_pageleave, or accept the paid tier as a decision; and correct the OPERATIONS.md '600k a year, no bill to reach' line so nobody trusts it at scale.
merged.gate: None (config/doc).

merged.title: Sentry sampling sized for today's traffic, not the target: 10% tracing is ~120k traces/month against a 10k-span free plan, and one hot-path bug exhausts the 5k error budget in ~3 hours
merged.reasoning: Verified from in-repo constants. instrumentation.ts:55-58 sets tracesSampleRate:0.1 with the in-code justification 'this site's traffic is tiny, so this stays comfortably inside' the 10,000-span free plan; OPERATIONS.md:118 confirms the free Developer plan is 5,000 errors and 10,000 spans a month. The justification inverts at the audit's mandated scale: even a few hundred daily-active members at ~20 views generate thousands of traced requests/month, and one traced request contains MANY spans (each DB query/function), so the finding's '12x even at one span per trace' is a conservative floor — the 10k-span budget is exhausted well before 2,000 users. Separately a 100%-reproduction hot-path error (the exact incident class instrumentation.ts:5-9 installed Sentry for) burns the 5,000-error/month budget in hours at scale. Consequence is graceful (Sentry sheds excess, no charge without a card) but observability goes dark exactly when the site is busiest. Low is correct; the fix is a one-line constant. Contingent on scale but arithmetic is deterministic from repo constants.
merged.repro: instrumentation.ts:58 tracesSampleRate=0.1, hard-coded, no dynamic sampling or beforeSend budget; OPERATIONS.md:118 the 10k-span/5k-error plan. 40k req/day x 0.1 x 30 = 120k traced requests/month >> 10k spans.
merged.fix: Lower tracesSampleRate to ~0.005-0.01 for launch and rely on Sentry server-side spike protection knowingly; keep errorSampleRate implicit at 1.0 but be aware of the 5k ceiling.
merged.gate: None (config).

merged.title: Type-ahead search limiter spends Upstash commands per keystroke; at target scale it can exhaust the free command quota, silently turning every rate limit off
merged.reasoning: Mechanism verified, bite is unpinned. rate-limit.ts:160 calls limiter.limit(key) per request on a slidingWindow (multi-command EVAL), and the search endpoints call it once per request (users/search/route.ts:29 rateLimit('search', session.user.id); places/search and users-by-batch exist alongside). Every limiter fails OPEN by deliberate design (rate-limit.ts:18-21 header + :162-165 catch returns {ok:true}), so IF Upstash's monthly command quota is exhausted, all throttles (login/signup/reset/trivia) silently switch off — a real security/DoS-protection gap during a busy month. But the finding itself is unsure of the quota ('500k/month as of 2025; verify the current number'), the whole consequence hinges on that number, and the command multiplier depends on whether the type-ahead client debounces keystrokes (not traced here). So this cannot be CONFIRMED without runtime numbers. Low.
merged.repro: N/A - needs live data.
merged.fix: N/A
merged.gate: N/A

newFindings.title: notifyReminder's 'shares the caller's transaction' comment is false for the nudgeGroup caller (deleteMany+createMany run non-atomically)
newFindings.reasoning: notifyReminder's docblock (catchups-notify.ts:154-156) claims 'Both statements share the caller's transaction, so a reader can never catch the gap where the old one is gone and the new one is not there yet.' That holds for the automatic caller applyEditionAction, which passes the transaction client (catchups.ts:1001). But nudgeGroup (actions.ts:2015) calls notifyReminder(prisma, ...) with the base client, so the deleteMany (catchups-notify.ts:186) and the createMany (:198) commit as two separate statements: a member polling the bell in the sub-second gap can momentarily see zero reminders. Real comment-vs-caller mismatch the finders missed; consequence is trivial (a millisecond gap in notification visibility on the manual-nudge path), hence Low. Fix: wrap the nudgeGroup call in prisma.$transaction so the claim the comment makes universally is actually true for every caller.

newFindings.title: Fresh-letter crash-net localStorage belt persists only content and title, not uploaded images or chosen audience
newFindings.reasoning: writeLocalDraft (create-post-form.tsx:240-251) serializes only { content, title, at }, and the restore path (:270-289) sets content and title only. A fresh letter (no row yet) that has had photos uploaded (images state holds R2 URLs) or an audience picked (audienceCity) and is then restored from the belt comes back with its images empty and audience cleared, so the writer silently loses the photo association and scope even when the belt itself fired. Adjacent to C-177 (same crash-net cluster) but a distinct gap the finders did not call out: the belt payload is narrower than the composer's persisted state. Low — the R2 objects still exist, only the draft's reference to them is lost, and it needs a fresh-letter-with-photos abandon-and-restore sequence.

newFindings.title: Fresh-letter crash-net localStorage (rv:letter-draft:new) is never cleared on publish or first save, so a later /letters/new restores already-published content and invites duplicate publishing
newFindings.reasoning: writeLocalDraft (lines 240-251) stores content+title under `rv:letter-draft:new` from the 2.5s idle effect (lines 263-267) whenever a fresh letter is being composed. clearLocalDraft (lines 252-259) is called from exactly ONE place — runAutosave success (line 348) — which only runs for a RESUMED draft (postId set) and clears the postId-based key, never ':new'. The createPost success paths (handleSubmit lines 706-748: both the publish branch and the onDraftSaved branch at 709-716) never call clearLocalDraft. So after a member composes a letter for >2.5s and publishes it, the ':new' entry survives; the next mount of /letters/new (restoredRef reset, initialContent undefined) hits the restore effect (lines 270-289) and reloads the just-published text with a 'Picked up where you left off' toast. The finders' C-014 only flagged the cross-account (unscoped-key) angle; this same-account stale-restore is a separate root cause (missing clear). Consequence on a normal path (compose -> publish -> revisit /letters/new): confusing restoration of already-public content and risk of an accidental duplicate publish.

newFindings.title: Share / Copy-link-to-post produces the same dead /feed#<id> anchor as the notification deep links (C-052 root cause, distinct user action)
newFindings.reasoning: The C-052 finder scoped the broken /feed#<id> anchor to notifications, but the same dead anchor is what the Share button copies: shareHref = `/feed#${post.id}` (post-card.tsx:221) is handed to ShareButton 'Copy link to post' (post-card.tsx:471). Since PostFeed never reads the hash and loads posts after mount (verified for C-052), a recipient who opens a copied share link lands at the top of /feed with the post unscrolled and, if it is older than the first page, absent entirely. This is a separate member action (sharing a link to a specific post) with the same broken result, so a C-052 fix that only touches notification links would leave Share broken. The repo's own lab finding feed-2 (src/app/lab/everything/_findings.ts) names this explicitly: 'That same dead link is what Share copies.' Fold Share (and the admin report-review link, which also uses postNotificationLink) into the same fix.

newFindings.title: Batch-range slider bounds (RangeFacetPill min/max) are computed from an aggregate that includes teacher batchYears, unlike the batch-tile counts that exclude them
newFindings.reasoning: batchYearRange (page.tsx:299-303) aggregates _min/_max batchYear over WHERE { isBlocked:false, deletionRequestedAt:null, batchYear:{ not:null } } with NO accountType exclusion, and feeds minBatchYear/maxBatchYear into the directory client's RangeFacetPill (page.tsx:377-378, directory-client.tsx:348-355). Every sibling batch surface deliberately excludes teachers: the batch-tile groupBy (page.tsx:292) and the faculty count (page.tsx:297). Combined with the C-095 root cause (a teacher/ex_teacher row can legitimately hold a batchYear via adminUpdatePerson), a single teacher with an out-of-range-for-alumni year (e.g. 1930) would skew the batch-range slider's min/max away from the actual alumni distribution, and filtering yearFrom to that bound would surface the teacher (buildDirectoryWhere batchYear clause has no accountType exclusion). Distinct surface from C-095's tile-count/Catch-ups claims. Low and data-dependent, but a real additional consequence the finders did not enumerate. Fix: add accountType notIn [teacher,ex_teacher] to the batchYearRange aggregate to match the tile counts.

newFindings.title: CSP img-src and connect-src carry the same over-broad '*.r2.dev' wildcard the codebase's own upload-shared.ts warns against
newFindings.reasoning: Related to C-134 but a distinct directive pair the C-134 finder did not call out: csp img-src (line 56) and connect-src (line 84) both list 'https://*.r2.dev', while upload-shared.ts:76-80 deliberately pins the ONE legacy host and its comment states 'a wildcard would vouch for [any bucket]'. The img-src wildcard lets the browser load images from any r2.dev bucket and connect-src lets it fetch from any r2.dev bucket (the photo-viewer Download path). This is low-value on its own (no injection vector to insert such a resource given script-src), but it is the same root inconsistency as C-134 and should be pinned to the exact legacy host in the same change for defense-in-depth consistency.

newFindings.title: gate-coverage and admin-page sweeps use git-tracked discovery, so a new UNTRACKED action/page escapes the pre-commit run
newFindings.reasoning: A fourth silent-skip vector in the same sweep as C-189, not listed by the finder. The action discovery at line 97 uses `git grep -l '"use server"'` and the admin-page sweep at line 157 uses `git ls-files` — both operate on git's tracked tree, not the working directory. `npm run check` is meant to run 'after any change and before every commit' (CLAUDE.md), i.e. typically before `git add`. A brand-new, not-yet-staged actions.ts with an ungated export, or a new untracked admin page.tsx that relies on the layout gate, is invisible to both sweeps and passes the local pre-commit run — the exact 'nobody thought about auth on a new endpoint' case the sweep exists to catch. Mitigated (hence Low): once the file is committed it becomes tracked, so the next local run and CI (which checks out the committed tree) both catch it. The window is the local working tree with an uncommitted new file, but that is precisely when a developer trusts the green check before committing.
